## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

# Long Term Vision + Goal

This project explores the most efficient ways to run a variety of AI/LLM generations on **Vulkan** using the AMD AI MAX+ 395 "Strix Halo" platform, with gfx1151 and RDNA3.5. 

Ultimately we want to be able to run these tasks:
  1. Speech to Text via Nvidia's `parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3`:
    * https://huggingface.co/nvidia/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3
    * https://arxiv.org/html/2509.14128v2
  2. Text generation via Qwen's `Qwen3.8-Next-Flash`:
    * https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next
    * https://arxiv.org/html/2608.30320v1
    * We'll need to quantise the weights once we've determined the most efficient method for the hardware
  3. Text to Speech via Hexgrad's `kokoro-82M`:
    * https://huggingface.co/hexgrad/Kokoro-82M
    * https://arxiv.org/html/2306.07691v2
  4. Image generation via Tongyi's `z-image-turbo`:
    * https://huggingface.co/Tongyi-MAI/Z-Image-Turbo
    * https://arxiv.org/html/2511.22699v5
    * With this smaller model to generate in-progress previews: 
      * https://huggingface.co/madebyollin/taef1
  5. Compute embeddings via Qwen's `Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B`:
    * https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B
    * https://arxiv.org/html/2506.05176v3

We will ultimately serve up a HTTP API serving these features, in Go.

pass, and now the three histories that make a second pass a continuation of

prefill graph down to 714.8** — 87.2% of it replaced by 61.4%, a 25.8% saving

253	      `ProfileSweep` walks a dispatch across layers and never re-reads a bank
254	      warm), against l8e's two-layer, 20-iteration fixture whose every GEMV
255	      down rung read **267-357 GB/s of a 242 GB/s bus**. Two runs agree to a
256	      median ratio of 0.9991 (p10-p90 0.982-1.012).
257	      `results/p1b_moe.csv`.
258	- [x] The ranking is unchanged: routed **v64w4/v16w4** (99.0 us at 186 GB/s,

260	      (13.4) win every marginal cold — the plan the model already runs. The
261	      MALL inflated magnitudes (down 34.4 → 59.3 us), not the order. D16's
262	      up-mode contradiction closes: cold, v16w4 loses to v64w4 by 1.15x, the
263	      same side as the whole model's 42.1 ms. And the router was never 3.5x

266	- [x] Gate: D16's test passes on the face of every rung — no row above 242
267	      GB/s — and the whole-model number is unchanged, as it must be when no
268	      rung changes: **32.78 tok/s, step 30.51 ms** (P1a measured 32.93),

272	      between a dispatch alone with a fence on a bank last read microseconds
273	      ago and the same dispatch in a 1407-dispatch buffer against a bank last
274	      read 4.3 GB ago. Bounded under P1c's 1.96 ms; written down, not chased.
275	      [Write-up](research/p1b-moe-decode-rescreen.md)
276	
277	### P1c — the pre-recorded decode command buffer  *(idea 2, now priced)*
278	
279	- [ ] **1.127 ms of recording plus 0.828 of hand-over: 6.4%, ~+2.2 tok/s.**
280	      The decode graph is shape-stable — same 1501 dispatches, same buffers,
281	      only the position and the token id change.
282	- [ ] Feed the varying scalars through a uniform buffer or indirect dispatch
283	      rather than re-recording.
284	- [ ] Gate: bit-identical tokens against the re-recording path over 128
285	      tokens, and the two host rows gone from `-gen -attrib`.
286	
287	### P2 — `ple_proj`, and close L8c  *(half a day; closes the stage)*
288	
289	- [ ] The last family: two 2560-wide matrices, no obstacle, two bank stages
290	      in one since `PLEGPU` never got the int8 bank either. 0.017 GB a
291	      token.
292	- [ ] Take D13's payoff: delete the two-plane fp16-tail machinery
293	      (`lowRank`/`gateOff` in the kernels, L8b-1's doubled rows) now that
294	      every tail is priced and the exception list is empty.
295	- [ ] Gate: bank-is-the-format equalities as at L8c-5/6/7, a 145-chunk
296	      corpus number for the **complete** uniform plan, and L8c closed in
297	      `LLM.md` with that number as the stage's result.
298	
299	### P3 — the shipped-widths decision  *(the knapsack, then D18)*
300	
301	- [ ] Sim-grade `q5_k` on `full_attn` (and, if cheap, on `lm_head` — the
302	      other expensive family) — no kernel needed to get the number.
303	- [ ] Pick the plan from measured corpus deltas: uniform 4.5 (+3.72%),
304	      `full_attn` at int8 (~+2.07%, −3.7 tok/s of ceiling), or `full_attn`
305	      at 5.5 bits if the sim says it earns its arm.
306	- [ ] Screen the winner on a second corpus and one small downstream eval
307	      (idea 5).
308	- [ ] Gate: a decision row **D18** with a 145-chunk number, and the served
309	      default set to it.

311	### P4 — the last bytes: the router and the experts  *(+4.5 tok/s of ceiling)*
312	
313	- [ ] The F32 router at fp16 (+1.5 of ceiling; L5a's tie analysis is the

315	- [ ] The expert banks toward ~4.25 bits (+3.0): transcode `ffn_down_exps`'s

321	      can be graded independently), decode measured in the whole model
322	      (D16: no ladder numbers), same text at temperature zero.

324	### P5 — MTP speculation  *(×1.5-1.8 on everything above; after P0, with idea 3's design)*
325	
326	- [ ] The rollback design doc first: state checkpointing, ring rewind, KV
327	      truncate, id-list rewind, and the M=2..8 verification-kernel
328	      decision.
329	- [ ] Then the draft head (2.79 GB GGUF, already downloaded) and the loop.
330	- [ ] Gate: **speculation is lossless** — token-for-token identical text at
331	      temperature zero — and a measured multiplier at ctx 512 *and* at a
332	      long context, because acceptance rates are context-dependent.
333	
334	### P6 — batching  *(pending the product question in idea 8)*
335	
336	- [ ] Decide whether the API serves concurrent streams; if yes, size the
337	      per-sequence state cost and the scheduler before optimising the

341	
342	W4A8 with the asymmetric epilogue (the GEMM arm is unmeasured); the unpack
343	prefetch (prefill lead, ~1.1x, "L8d's third lead"); the fp16 residual; the
344	hot-expert fast path; the float-atomic combine; the vision tower; the
345	llama.cpp rebuild question (a rebuild invalidates trace and baseline
346	together).
347	
348	---
349	
350	## Why this order
351	
352	**P0, P1, P1a and P1b are done, and each of them moved the list.** P1's suspicion —
353	that the bank had stopped being the binding constraint — is confirmed, and
354	the replacement is **kernel shape**: four of the five leading items are
355	dispatches that are too small or the wrong way round, not bytes.
356	
357	**P1a then sharpened what "too small" means, and it is not what the phrase
358	suggested.** Fusing the weightless half of the hyper-connection boundary was
359	worth its estimate (+0.34 tok/s, 94 dispatches, bit-exact); the *bank* half
360	was not a fusion question at all. A one-token dispatch on this device is
361	short of **workgroups**, and the down projection's own decode ladder measures
362	the law on identical bytes: **168 workgroups is 9.26 us where 672 is 5.54**.
363	`up` sits at 160 workgroups because MODE 1's collapse pins `BN` at 64, and
364	unpinning it is priced at 0.22 ms a token — real, and not worth every rung's
365	epilogue on the prefill path.
366	
367	**P1b looked like the largest item on the list by a factor of four, and it
368	was the MALL's arithmetic.** The one-token MoE ladder those rungs were chosen
369	from was an L3 measurement end to end (every GEMV down rung above the bus);

371	1.9 ms was never there. What is there is a **1.33 ms environment gap** — the
372	same dispatch is 8-22% slower inside a real step than alone on a cold bank —
373	which P1c's pre-recorded command buffer may eat part of, since barriers and

377	small. P5 is the largest single multiplier on the list but wants its own

379	it loses nothing by going after.
380	
381	**The numbers to beat from here: 32.93 tok/s measured, 53.0 honest ceiling
382	on today's bank at the 227 GB/s dispatches reach — so the step is **62%**
383	efficient and the gap is itemised — and llama.cpp at 25.15, already behind at

# LLM2 — the review, the hypotheses checked, and the next priority list

> **Written 2026-09-17**, as a review of `LLM.md` at L8c-7 / L9a. `LLM.md`
> stays the stage log; this file is the forward-looking list. Same
> conventions: history to `TODO.md`, closed findings to `research/`.

## Where this stands, in five lines

- **Decode 32.93 tok/s** against llama.cpp's 25.15 — **1.31x** — at a
  measured bank of 4.281 GB a token, a ceiling of 56.5 at the bus and 53.0
  at the rate dispatches reach. P1 attributed the step to the dispatch and
  took the n-gram gather's sixteen serialised page faults out of it; P1a
  fused the hyper-connection boundary, 1501 dispatches a pass to 1407.
- **Prefill 1089.2 tok/s** at ubatch 2048 against 391.4 — **2.78x** — and
  668.1 at 512. The original L2a target of ~1150 is 95% reached. P1a's fusion
  is +1.7% of it at 2048 and nothing at 512, because the residual crosses the
  MALL in between.
- **Perplexity 4.1787 against our 4.0289 — +3.72%** (and +3.59% against the
  reference's own 4.0340), with five of six dense families at 4.5 bits and
  additivity holding to 0.01 pp.
- **Served**: `cmd/serve -llm`, three envelopes over one loop, prefix reuse.
- ~~**One correctness cliff**~~: **closed at P0 (2026-09-18)**. It was
  amdgpu's gfx ring watchdog killing any submit that holds the ring past
  **2 s** — not rows, layers, bytes or residency. The recorder chunks by time
  now, and prefill runs to **8192 rows at 1213.5 tok/s, 3.10x**, still
  climbing where llama.cpp's plateaus.

Phase 1 is done, phase 2's kernel half is done, and phase 2's width half is
one trivial family (`ple_proj`) from done. The plan as originally drawn —
run it, profile it, then optimise — executed, and the reference is beaten on
both axes. **The competition from here is our own ceiling, not llama.cpp.**

---

## The hypotheses, checked

| hypothesis | verdict |
|---|---|
| **"Decode is DRAM-bound by weight bytes"** (the premise of D3, L8a-L8c) | **Was true, is now 79% true, and P1 says where the rest is.** Through L8b, measured ≈ ceiling: 14.71 tok/s against 15.4 GB-derived numbers. Today the weight-streaming dispatches are **24.05 ms of a 30.52 ms step, 79%** — but they run at **178 GB/s against the 227 a dispatch reaches**, so 5.54 ms of that is shape rather than bytes, and another 3.46 ms of dispatches stream no weight at all. The binding constraint has moved from *how many bytes* to *how the dispatches are shaped*: `hyper_conn` at 114.6 GB/s and `moe.down` at 147.5 against `moe.up`'s 200.6 off the same bank. |
| **"The cost of 4 bits runs inverse to the bytes"** (L8c-1's headline) | **Retired by its own successors.** The pp-per-GB ranking over 145 chunks is bimodal: `deltanet` 0.87, `hyper_conn` 0.93, `lm_head` 2.59, `full_attn` 5.52 — and the split is presence (36 layers / 97 mixers vs 12 layers / 1 matrix), not size. |
| **"An 8-chunk screen predicts a family's corpus cost"** | **Retired, four ways.** +0.40→+0.82, −0.30→+0.93, +0.90→+0.31, +1.05→+1.65. A screen does not bound, does not fix the sign, does not rank. Every future width call needs a 145-chunk run (8 min — affordable). |
| **"Corpus deltas add"** (the asymmetric form's additivity) | **Confirmed to 0.01 pp across four families** — where the symmetric form compounded 11.7% into 18.5%. This is now a *tool*: plans are composable from measured per-family deltas (see idea 4). Caveat: only demonstrated on the asymmetric form at 4.5 bits. |
| **D14: "a bank that fits the MALL pays only its unpack"** | **Confirmed with its boundary, four blocks, both signs, one rule.** Closed as a hypothesis; it is now a design fact. |
| **D12's 4 KB formulation** | **Weakened at L8c-6** (no rung is a whole multiple and the spread is still 1.65x); the operative half — *re-measure when the width changes* — stands and is what caught it. |
| **"Residency is free"** (L6a-4) | **Confirmed at ≤2560 rows — and the >2560 stall is plausibly its boundary.** The untested suspicion in the open question is exactly residency (~80 GB pinned + 28.8 GB mmap + arenas that grow with rows). If P0 confirms it, L6a-4 gains a cliff. |
| **"Context is cheap here"** (the QSA table in `LLM.md`) | **Priced, never demonstrated.** The arithmetic says 6.8 GB of KV at 262k and a capped 2051-cell read per step; the graph has never completed past 2560 rows. Currently an *inference*, not a measurement — P0 gates it. |
| **D16: a rung above 242 GB/s is not a DRAM measurement** | **Confirmed and generalising**: every one-token ladder screened so far was choosing rungs against an L3 hit. Standing rule: re-screen a ladder before acting on it. |

---

## The decode budget, re-derived honestly

The 56.5 tok/s ceiling counts streamed weights only. A token also moves:

    DeltaNet state, 36 x 3.1 MB, read + write     ~0.22 GB
    KV + indexer at 2k context                    ~0.05 GB
    activations, rings, logits row                ~0.01 GB
                                                  --------
    honest per-token traffic                      ~4.56 GB  -> ~53 tok/s

Measured 31.5 tok/s is 31.7 ms a token; 4.56 GB at the best measured
dispatch rate (227 GB/s) is ~20 ms. **~12 ms a token — 37% of the step — is
not accounted for by streaming bytes at any achievable rate**, and no
attribution has been run since L8e.

**P1 ran it, and the estimate was right to 0.01 ms.** The step is 30.52 ms
after the gather fix, and it sums:

    weight-streaming dispatches, 4.281 GB at 178 GB/s      24.05 ms
      of which, over the 18.86 ms the same bytes take at 227   5.54
    dispatches that stream no weight (scan, moves, norms,
      permutations, combines)                               3.46 ms
    host: record 1.127, gather 0.902, hand-over 0.828,
      sample 0.142, detokenize + emit 0.007                 3.01 ms
    unattributed                                            0.005 ms

**5.54 + 3.46 + 3.01 = 12.01.** The candidates list above was almost exactly
wrong in its ordering: the sampler and detokenizer are **0.15 ms together**,
host record and submit are 1.96, and the two real items are dispatches off
the bus (`hyper_conn` at 114.6 GB/s, `moe.down` at 147.5) and the 3.46 ms of
dispatches nobody had counted because they read no weights at all. The one
candidate that was under-rated is the PLE host gather, which was 2.24 ms and
is now 0.90 — see P1's finding 1.

---

## Ideas that are not in the current plan

1. ~~**Re-attribute the decode step**~~ **— done (P1), and it was the single
   highest information-per-hour item on the list**: it paid for itself with
   the gather fix before the analysis was written, and it demoted idea 2
   from first to fourth.
2. **A pre-recorded, reusable decode command buffer.** IDEAS §4.2 was never
   carried into this vertical. The decode graph is shape-stable token to
   token — **1501 dispatches** (P1 counted them; the ~490 here was the
   pre-L7d submit count), same buffers; only the position and the token id
   change. Record once, feed the varying scalars through a small uniform
   buffer (or indirect dispatch) instead of re-recording. **P1 priced it:
   1.127 ms of recording plus 0.828 of hand-over, 6.4% of the step, about
   +2.2 tok/s** — real, and, with P1a done and P1b measured empty, now the
   front of the list.
3. **MTP needs a rollback story before it needs a kernel.** Speculation on a
   *recurrent* model is not the usual KV-truncate: a rejected draft must
   rewind (a) 36 DeltaNet states — checkpoint/restore of 113 MB, ~0.3 ms as
   a device copy, fine but must be designed in; (b) both convolution rings,
   whose stores are currently pure writes addressed by position; (c) the KV
   cache and pooled indexer blocks (easy — truncate); (d) the host-side id
   list the trigram hash reads. And verification runs at M = 2-8, where D15
   *refuses* the GEMV path by design — the M=2..8 GEMM/GEMV crossover
   (IDEAS §1.5) has never been measured on this model's shapes. A half-page
   design doc first; it changes the state-object API (P5).
4. **The accuracy knapsack.** Additivity + per-family corpus deltas mean the
   shipped plan is now a solvable trade, and the uniform plan is provably
   not optimal in pp-per-GB: `full_attn` buys 0.299 GB a token for +1.65%
   while `deltanet` buys 1.07 GB for +0.93%. Two composable options, both
   computable *today* from numbers already in `results/`:
   - `full_attn` back to int8: ~4.58 GB a token, ~52.8 ceiling, **~+2.07%**.
   - `full_attn` at 5.5 bits: `sim.go` can grade a q5_k arm in one 8-min
     run **before any kernel exists** — likely most of the bytes back for a
     fraction of the 1.65.
   Nothing forces uniform 4.5. Decide with numbers, record it as D18.
5. **A second corpus, and one downstream eval.** +3.72% rests entirely on
   wikitext-2. The instrument is corpus-agnostic — one run on code or on
   chat-formatted text is 8 minutes — and the HTTP API makes a small
   task-level screen (a few hundred multiple-choice items) an evening. Cheap
   insurance before the widths are declared shipped.
6. **The DeltaNet state's width.** 0.22 GB a token of the honest budget is
   f32 state traffic. fp16 state halves it (+~1.3 tok/s of ceiling) — but
   the recurrence accumulates, which is exactly where fp16 goes wrong.
   Gradeable end-to-end with the ppl instrument; low priority, but it is
   the only remaining per-token traffic nobody has named as a lever.
7. **Long-context gates, the day P0 lands**: perplexity at ctx 8k with the
   selection biting hard, decode tok/s flatness against context (QSA's
   whole promise), and a needle test through the API. None exist because
   none *can* yet.
8. **Batching × recurrence.** "Batching amortises the dense 76%" is carried
   from the phase-3 sketch, but each concurrent sequence owns 113 MB of
   DeltaNet state, its own rings and its own KV — the served graph is one
   sequence's today. The open product question ("will the API ever serve
   more than one stream?") should be answered before P5/P6 ordering is
   final, because if yes, batching may beat MTP for the same effort.
9. ~~**Reconcile the 0.38 GB**~~ **— closed at P1.** It is the MoE router
   (0.252 GB) and the shared expert (0.251), which the checkpoint inventory
   files under "dense, every token" and L8b's table files with the MoE, less
   L8b-1's doubled `inject` rows, `PLEGPU`'s halves and rounding. Both
   counts were right; they partitioned the same tensors differently. Every
   ceiling is now quoted on **4.281 GB a token**.

---

## The priority list

### ~~P0 — the >2560-row stall~~  *(**done**, 2026-09-18)*

**It was amdgpu's gfx ring watchdog, and none of the four hypotheses above.**
A submit that holds the gfx ring past **2.0 s** is killed and the ring reset;
the reset *force-signals the fence*, so `vkQueueSubmit` and `vkWaitForFences`
both return success and the spin is six lines later, in
`vkGetQueryPoolResults(VK_QUERY_RESULT_WAIT_BIT)` — an unbounded **userspace**
poll on RADV, of a timestamp the killed dispatches never wrote. `[syscall]` in
the old dump was Go's label for a cgo call: `utime=5645` against `stime=5`.
Full write-up: [research/p0-ring-watchdog.md](research/p0-ring-watchdog.md).

- [x] Reproduce and look at the kernel side. `/proc/<pid>/stack` and debugfs
      both want root here; `/proc/<tid>/stat` and `journalctl -k` did the job
      instead, and a native backtrace needed gdb to be the *ancestor*
      (`ptrace_scope` 1).
- [x] Bisect the cliff's shape. It tracks **neither** rows nor layers nor
      bytes: 1024 dispatches is 1.886 s at 2560 rows and runs, 1.964 s at 2688
      and runs, **2.033 s at 2816 and is reset**. GTT, VRAM and RSS are flat
      through the whole stall, so this is **not** L6a-4's boundary and
      "residency is free" comes out unmarked rather than confirmed.
- [x] The C ABI audit was not needed: the control settles it. The same 1273
      dispatches in one submit are 787 ms at 512 rows and fine, and are reset
      at 2688 rows where two submits of the same work had just run.
- [x] Control: smaller command buffers complete. 3072 rows in five submits of
      256 runs at 1143.1 tok/s.
- [x] **Fix**: the recorder chunks by *time* (`batchFor`), from an affine fit
      of 322 us a dispatch plus 582 ns a dispatch-row, budgeted at half the
      cliff. Decode is untouched (1 row still batches at 1024). The shim's
      query reads all go through a deadline that names the missing slots
      instead of spinning.
- [x] **Gate**: `-graph` returns at 4096 (**1174.6 tok/s, 3.00x**) and 8192
      (**1213.5, 3.10x**, at `-ctx 8192`); `-ppl -ctx 4096` completes at 48
      layers at **PPL 3.9392 +/- 0.02209** over 72 chunks of 4096, against
      4.0289 for the same bank at n_ctx 2048 — twice the context is **-2.23%**
      with the selection live, which is idea 7's first gate. Prefill **does not
      plateau** where llama.cpp's does.
- [ ] Carried forward: idea 7's remaining long-context gates — perplexity at
      ctx 8192, decode tok/s against context, and a needle test through the
      API — are now possible and are not yet run.

### ~~P1 — re-attribute the decode step~~  *(**done**, 2026-09-18)*

- [x] Per-dispatch timestamps over 64 decode steps on today's bank, plus
      the host side split — **the table sums to 30.52 ms with a 5 us
      residual**, over 36 dispatch labels and six host phases.
      `-gen -attrib`, `results/p1_decode_attrib.csv`.
- [x] Reconcile the 0.38 GB (idea 9): **it is the MoE router (0.252) and the
      shared expert (0.251)**, which the checkpoint inventory files under
      "dense, every token" and L8b's table files with the MoE, less three
      doublings in the other column. Every ceiling is now quoted on
      **4.281 GB a token**.
- [x] Act on anything ≥1 ms with a known fix: **the PLE gather, 2.244 ms,
      was sixteen serialised major page faults a token** — not compute, not
      bytes. Concurrent: identical fault count (16.3), **7.0-7.5x**,
      2.244 → 0.902 ms, **decode 31.51 → 32.72 tok/s**. The rest is written
      down as P1a-P1c below.
- [x] Gate: the gap is named. **12.01 ms = 5.54 (weight-streaming dispatches
      below 227 GB/s) + 3.46 (dispatches that stream no weight) + 3.01
      (host)**, and idea 2 — the review's favourite for the whole of it — is
      **1.96 ms** and now ranks fourth. [Write-up](research/p1-decode-attribution.md)

### ~~P1a — the hyper-connection block's 485 dispatches~~  *(**done**, 2026-09-18)*

**The weightless half is fused away bit-exactly; the other half is a grid,
and the grid is priced rather than rebuilt.**

- [x] The scatter that closes one mixer and the norm that opens the next are
      the same 2560 values per (token, stream) written and read straight
      back, and both were already one workgroup per (token, stream).
      `llm_hc_cn.comp` does both in one pass over registers: **1501
      dispatches a pass to 1407, 30.69 ms to 30.37, decode 32.59 → 32.93
      tok/s**, both arms on one build (`LLM_HC_NOFUSE=1` is the control).
      **Prefill comes along at ubatch 2048 — 1070.8 → 1089.2 tok/s, +1.7%,
      the block 330.1 → 294.6 ms** — where the fusion removes an 84 MB read a
      boundary; at 512 it is worth nothing, because 21 MB fits the MALL.
- [x] **Identical to the last place** on `res`, `xn` and `mixed`
      (`TestHCFusionIsTheCombineThenTheNorm`, `TestHCFusionRunsThePass`).
      The ulp chased first: giving the sum a *second reader* lets ACO
      contract it into an FMA where the scatter rounds twice, and `precise`
      is the only thing that says no.
- [x] Gate: the label count moved and **the GB/s did not** — 114.9 against
      114.6 — and the ladder says why. The down projection's decode rungs
      read the same 1.94 MB off the same bank with a grid that varies
      twenty-fold, and **168 workgroups is 9.26 us where 672 is 5.54**. So
      `up_m1`'s 10.87 us at **160 workgroups** is not MODE 1's M=1 waste; it
      is `down_gemv8`'s number at `down_gemv8`'s width.
- [ ] Carried forward, priced and not taken: `BN` cannot fall below 64 in
      MODE 1 because `packUpB` makes a 64-column block 16 features x 4
      streams. A 4x4 block would be 640 workgroups, worth **2.3 us a mixer,
      0.22 ms a token, +0.24 tok/s** — and it is every `up` rung's epilogue
      on the prefill path, so 0.7% of decode does not buy it.
      [Write-up](research/p1a-hyper-connection-shape.md)

### ~~P1b — `moe.down`'s rung, and the shared expert's~~  *(**done**, 2026-09-18 — a ladder, and no rung moves)*

**The 1.19 + 0.73 ms was the MALL's arithmetic. Re-screened against DRAM the
plan survives on every axis, and what is real is a 1.33 ms environment gap
that is not a rung choice.**

- [x] The ladder, honest: **sixteen cold banks at `-iters 1`** (25.6 GB, so
      `ProfileSweep` walks a dispatch across layers and never re-reads a bank
      warm), against l8e's two-layer, 20-iteration fixture whose every GEMV
      down rung read **267-357 GB/s of a 242 GB/s bus**. Two runs agree to a
      median ratio of 0.9991 (p10-p90 0.982-1.012).
      `results/p1b_moe.csv`.
- [x] The ranking is unchanged: routed **v64w4/v16w4** (99.0 us at 186 GB/s,
      59.3 at 207), shared **v64w4/v32w4** (22.7, 10.9), router **k40**
      (13.4) win every marginal cold — the plan the model already runs. The
      MALL inflated magnitudes (down 34.4 → 59.3 us), not the order. D16's
      up-mode contradiction closes: cold, v16w4 loses to v64w4 by 1.15x, the
      same side as the whole model's 42.1 ms. And the router was never 3.5x
      off — its 4.4 us ladder rate was two fp16 router matrices in the MALL;
      cold it is 13.4-14.8 against 15.1 in the model.
- [x] Gate: D16's test passes on the face of every rung — no row above 242
      GB/s — and the whole-model number is unchanged, as it must be when no
      rung changes: **32.78 tok/s, step 30.51 ms** (P1a measured 32.93),
      `results/p1b_decode_attrib.csv`. What the honest floors expose is a
      **1.33 ms a token environment gap** — moe.down 72.2 us in the model
      against 59.3 alone-and-cold (1.22x), the other four labels 1.08-1.16x —
      between a dispatch alone with a fence on a bank last read microseconds
      ago and the same dispatch in a 1407-dispatch buffer against a bank last
      read 4.3 GB ago. Bounded under P1c's 1.96 ms; written down, not chased.
      [Write-up](research/p1b-moe-decode-rescreen.md)

### P1c — the pre-recorded decode command buffer  *(idea 2, now priced)*

- [ ] **1.127 ms of recording plus 0.828 of hand-over: 6.4%, ~+2.2 tok/s.**
      The decode graph is shape-stable — same 1501 dispatches, same buffers,
      only the position and the token id change.
- [ ] Feed the varying scalars through a uniform buffer or indirect dispatch
      rather than re-recording.
- [ ] Gate: bit-identical tokens against the re-recording path over 128
      tokens, and the two host rows gone from `-gen -attrib`.

### P2 — `ple_proj`, and close L8c  *(half a day; closes the stage)*

- [ ] The last family: two 2560-wide matrices, no obstacle, two bank stages
      in one since `PLEGPU` never got the int8 bank either. 0.017 GB a
      token.
- [ ] Take D13's payoff: delete the two-plane fp16-tail machinery
      (`lowRank`/`gateOff` in the kernels, L8b-1's doubled rows) now that
      every tail is priced and the exception list is empty.
- [ ] Gate: bank-is-the-format equalities as at L8c-5/6/7, a 145-chunk
      corpus number for the **complete** uniform plan, and L8c closed in
      `LLM.md` with that number as the stage's result.

### P3 — the shipped-widths decision  *(the knapsack, then D18)*

- [ ] Sim-grade `q5_k` on `full_attn` (and, if cheap, on `lm_head` — the
      other expensive family) — no kernel needed to get the number.
- [ ] Pick the plan from measured corpus deltas: uniform 4.5 (+3.72%),
      `full_attn` at int8 (~+2.07%, −3.7 tok/s of ceiling), or `full_attn`
      at 5.5 bits if the sim says it earns its arm.
- [ ] Screen the winner on a second corpus and one small downstream eval
      (idea 5).
- [ ] Gate: a decision row **D18** with a 145-chunk number, and the served
      default set to it.

### P4 — the last bytes: the router and the experts  *(+4.5 tok/s of ceiling)*

- [ ] The F32 router at fp16 (+1.5 of ceiling; L5a's tie analysis is the
      named risk — check the top-10 sets over a real prompt, not just ppl).
- [ ] The expert banks toward ~4.25 bits (+3.0): transcode `ffn_down_exps`'s
      Q5_1 (27.1 GB) and the five Q8_0 layers to Q4_K with the imatrix —
      **the existing `llm_moe_gemm/gemv` arms already read Q4_K**, so this
      is a transcode and a corpus run, not a kernel. L8c-3 is the reason to
      expect the calibrated form to behave; D4 (nothing below 4 bits) holds.
- [ ] Gate: 145-chunk ppl for each step separately (additivity says they
      can be graded independently), decode measured in the whole model
      (D16: no ladder numbers), same text at temperature zero.

### P5 — MTP speculation  *(×1.5-1.8 on everything above; after P0, with idea 3's design)*

- [ ] The rollback design doc first: state checkpointing, ring rewind, KV
      truncate, id-list rewind, and the M=2..8 verification-kernel
      decision.
- [ ] Then the draft head (2.79 GB GGUF, already downloaded) and the loop.
- [ ] Gate: **speculation is lossless** — token-for-token identical text at
      temperature zero — and a measured multiplier at ctx 512 *and* at a
      long context, because acceptance rates are context-dependent.

### P6 — batching  *(pending the product question in idea 8)*

- [ ] Decide whether the API serves concurrent streams; if yes, size the
      per-sequence state cost and the scheduler before optimising the
      batch-1 path further.

### Parked (unchanged from `LLM.md`, in one place)

W4A8 with the asymmetric epilogue (the GEMM arm is unmeasured); the unpack
prefetch (prefill lead, ~1.1x, "L8d's third lead"); the fp16 residual; the
hot-expert fast path; the float-atomic combine; the vision tower; the
llama.cpp rebuild question (a rebuild invalidates trace and baseline
together).

---

## Why this order

**P0, P1, P1a and P1b are done, and each of them moved the list.** P1's suspicion —
that the bank had stopped being the binding constraint — is confirmed, and
the replacement is **kernel shape**: four of the five leading items are
dispatches that are too small or the wrong way round, not bytes.

**P1a then sharpened what "too small" means, and it is not what the phrase
suggested.** Fusing the weightless half of the hyper-connection boundary was
worth its estimate (+0.34 tok/s, 94 dispatches, bit-exact); the *bank* half
was not a fusion question at all. A one-token dispatch on this device is
short of **workgroups**, and the down projection's own decode ladder measures
the law on identical bytes: **168 workgroups is 9.26 us where 672 is 5.54**.
`up` sits at 160 workgroups because MODE 1's collapse pins `BN` at 64, and
unpinning it is priced at 0.22 ms a token — real, and not worth every rung's
epilogue on the prefill path.

**P1b looked like the largest item on the list by a factor of four, and it
was the MALL's arithmetic.** The one-token MoE ladder those rungs were chosen
from was an L3 measurement end to end (every GEMV down rung above the bus);
re-run on sixteen cold banks the ranking does not move on any axis, so the
1.9 ms was never there. What is there is a **1.33 ms environment gap** — the
same dispatch is 8-22% slower inside a real step than alone on a cold bank —
which P1c's pre-recorded command buffer may eat part of, since barriers and
buffer hand-over are half of the suspects. **That promotes P1c to the front
of the list.** P2 and P3 still close the
accuracy story while additivity and the instruments are warm, and they are
small. P5 is the largest single multiplier on the list but wants its own
design pass, and its multiplier applies on top of whatever the rest buys, so
it loses nothing by going after.

**The numbers to beat from here: 32.93 tok/s measured, 53.0 honest ceiling
on today's bank at the 227 GB/s dispatches reach — so the step is **62%**
efficient and the gap is itemised — and llama.cpp at 25.15, already behind at
every ubatch.**

1	package llm
2	
3	// One command buffer a **pass**, and the attribution that has to survive it:
4	// LLM.md L7d.
5	//
6	// L7c-5 took the graph from a submit a dispatch to a submit a block — ~1130
7	// to ~490 — and priced the rest at 31-43 us each, which is ~15-21 ms of a
8	// 99 ms decode token. Nothing in the shim ever prevented going further: it
9	// binds each dispatch's own pipeline, descriptor set and push constants, so a
10	// sequence may mix blocks as freely as it mixes kernels of one block. What
11	// stopped it was the *measurement*. Every number this vertical has been tuned
12	// by comes from the host wall clock around a block's `Run`, and a block that
13	// no longer submits has no wall clock of its own.
14	//
15	// So the recorder moves both. Each block's `Run` appends to it instead of
16	// submitting when one is installed, and the submit asks the shim for a
17	// timestamp after **every** dispatch (vk.DispatchMultiMarked) rather than only
18	// at the two ends. The per-block figures that come back are then GPU time
19	// inside one command buffer rather than host time around many, which is the
20	// same thing llama.cpp's own `GGML_VK_PERF_LOGGER` reports for its graph — the
21	// baseline half of every comparison in LLM.md — and strictly the better
22	// number: it cannot be inflated by a fence wait, a Go allocation or a page
23	// fault on the host.
24	
25	import (
26		"fmt"
27		"os"
28		"strconv"
29		"strings"
30		"time"
31	
32		"strix-halo-vulkan/vk"
33	)
34	
35	// The block names a dispatch can be attributed to. They are the rows of
36	// GraphStats, and a dispatch carries one because a command buffer does not.
37	const (
38		ownHC   = "hc"
39		ownPLE  = "ple"
40		ownDN   = "dn"
41		ownAttn = "attn"
42		ownMoE  = "moe"
43		ownHead = "head"
44		ownMove = "move"
45	)
46	
47	// maxBatch is how many dispatches go into one command buffer. It is a bound
48	// on the shim's query pool (SHIM_QUERY_SLOTS) and not a tuning knob: a whole
49	// prefill pass is ~1200 dispatches, so this is one submit for a decode token
50	// and two for a long prompt, against the ~490 either used to take.
51	// LLM_MAX_BATCH overrides it, which is how P0 asked whether a hang was about
52	// the size of one submit rather than about any dispatch in it.
53	var maxBatch = envInt("LLM_MAX_BATCH", 1024)
54	
55	// minBatch keeps the row-scaled bound below from degenerating: a submit costs
56	// ~40 us, so even at 32 dispatches the boundary is under 2% of a pass.
57	const minBatch = 32
58	
59	// submitBudget is how much GPU time one command buffer may hold.
60	//
61	// **P0.** It is not the query pool and it is not the dispatch count: a submit
62	// that occupies the gfx ring for more than ~2 s is killed by amdgpu's ring
63	// watchdog. The kernel says `ring gfx_0.0.0 timeout, signaled seq=N, emitted
64	// seq=N+3`, resets the ring, and the reset *force-signals the fence* -- so
65	// vkQueueSubmit returns, vkWaitForFences returns VK_SUCCESS, its own 20-second
66	// timeout never fires, and the only trace left is the timestamps the killed
67	// dispatches never wrote. Reading those with VK_QUERY_RESULT_WAIT_BIT is an
68	// unbounded userspace poll inside RADV, which is the 100%-of-a-core spin that
69	// looked like a hang in the submit (see shim_query_results_deadline).
70	//
71	// Measured at 48 layers, 1024 dispatches a submit: 2560 rows is 1.886 s and
72	// runs, 2688 rows is 1.964 s and runs, 2816 rows is 2.033 s and is reset. The
73	// same 1273 dispatches in *one* submit are 787 ms at 512 rows and run, and are
74	// reset at 2688 rows -- where two submits of 1024 and 249 had just run the same
75	// work. So the bound is time, and half the cliff is the budget.
76	const submitBudget = 1000 * time.Millisecond
77	
78	// A pass's cost is affine in the rows, not proportional to them: fitting the
79	// whole-pass figures of 789.5 ms at 512 rows, 2342.4 at 2560, 2434.2 at 2688
80	// and 2687.5 at 3072 over 1273 dispatches gives 322 us a dispatch plus 582 ns
81	// a dispatch-row, and predicts all four to within 1.5%. It puts a 1024-dispatch
82	// submit at 2816 rows at 2.008 s, which is the row count that is reset.
83	const (
84		usPerDispatch    = 322
85		nsPerDispatchRow = 582
86	)
87	
88	// dispatchCost is what one dispatch of a pass over this many rows costs.
89	func dispatchCost(rows int) time.Duration {
90		return usPerDispatch*time.Microsecond + time.Duration(nsPerDispatchRow*rows)*time.Nanosecond
91	}
92	
93	// batchFor is how many dispatches fit in submitBudget at this many rows. At
94	// one row -- every decode step -- it is maxBatch, so nothing about decode
95	// changes; it starts biting at ~1700 rows and is ~200 at 8192.
96	func batchFor(rows int) int {
97		if rows < 1 {
98			rows = 1
99		}
100		n := int(submitBudget / dispatchCost(rows))
101		return min(max(n, minBatch), maxBatch)
102	}
103	
104	// BatchFor is that bound at a given number of rows, exported for a caller
105	// reporting how many command buffers a pass took.
106	func BatchFor(rows int) int { return batchFor(rows) }
107	
108	// batchTimes prints each submit's GPU time, which is how the budget above is
109	// checked against the ring rather than against the model that predicts it.
110	var batchTimes = os.Getenv("LLM_BATCH_TIMES") != ""
111	
112	func envInt(name string, def int) int {
113		if v, err := strconv.Atoi(os.Getenv(name)); err == nil && v > 0 {
114			return v
115		}
116		return def
117	}
118	
119	// recorder collects a pass's dispatches with the block each came from.
120	type recorder struct {
121		d     []vk.MultiDispatch
122		owner []string
123		// kind is the block's own name for each dispatch -- "moe.up",
124		// "attn.qkv" -- which is what P1 needed and what every block's `graph`
125		// method has always built for its error messages. A block name is where
126		// the time is *not*: the MoE is 11.6 ms of a 31.7 ms token and says
127		// nothing about which of its nine kernels that is.
128		kind []string
129		// rows is what the pass is passing, which is what a dispatch's cost --
130		// and so how many of them fit in one submit -- scales with.
131		rows int
132	}
133	
134	// add appends one block's sequence, with the block's own label per dispatch.
135	// A nil recorder is the direct path, which is what every block does when the
136	// graph is not batching and what the per-block benchmarks always do.
137	//
138	// `kinds` may be shorter than `d` or nil -- the mover has one dispatch and no
139	// label of its own -- in which case the owner's name stands in.
140	func (r *recorder) add(owner string, kinds []string, d []vk.MultiDispatch) bool {
141		if r == nil {
142			return false
143		}
144		r.d = append(r.d, d...)
145		for i := range d {
146			r.owner = append(r.owner, owner)
147			k := owner
148			if i < len(kinds) {
149				k = owner + "." + kinds[i]
150			}
151			r.kind = append(r.kind, k)
152		}
153		return true
154	}
155	
156	func (r *recorder) len() int {
157		if r == nil {
158			return 0
159		}
160		return len(r.d)
161	}
162	
163	// DispatchStat is one kernel's share of a pass: how many dispatches carried
164	// that label and what they cost on the GPU.
165	type DispatchStat struct {
166		Count int
167		GPU   time.Duration
168	}
169	
170	// submit runs everything recorded, in order, and returns the GPU time each
171	// block's dispatches took, and the same split by the label each carried. It
172	// chunks at batchFor(rows), which costs one more fence wait per chunk and
173	// keeps the marks.
174	func (r *recorder) submit() (map[string]time.Duration, map[string]DispatchStat, time.Duration, error) {
175		byOwner := make(map[string]time.Duration, 8)
176		byKind := make(map[string]DispatchStat, 64)
177		var total time.Duration
178		r.dumpRange()
179		batch := batchFor(r.rows)
180		for i := 0; i < len(r.d); i += batch {
181			j := minInt(i+batch, len(r.d))
182			el, each, err := vk.DispatchMultiMarked(r.d[i:j], true)
183			if err != nil {
184				return nil, nil, 0, fmt.Errorf("llm: dispatches %d-%d: %w", i, j-1, err)
185			}
186			if batchTimes {
187				fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "batch %d-%d: %v on the GPU\n", i, j-1, el)
188			}
189			total += el
190			if each == nil {
191				// The shim refused the marks, which at this size it cannot; the
192				// pass still ran, so report it as one block rather than losing it.
193				byOwner[r.owner[i]] += el
194				s := byKind[r.kind[i]]
195				s.Count, s.GPU = s.Count+j-i, s.GPU+el
196				byKind[r.kind[i]] = s
197				continue
198			}
199			for k, d := range each {
200				byOwner[r.owner[i+k]] += d
201				s := byKind[r.kind[i+k]]
202				s.Count, s.GPU = s.Count+1, s.GPU+d
203				byKind[r.kind[i+k]] = s
204			}
205		}
206		r.d, r.owner, r.kind = r.d[:0], r.owner[:0], r.kind[:0]
207		return byOwner, byKind, total, nil
208	}
209	
210	// dumpRange prints the block and grid of a slice of the recorded sequence
211	// before it is submitted, which is the only moment a dispatch that hangs the
212	// GPU can still be named. LLM_DISPATCH_DUMP=lo:hi selects the range; the
213	// dispatch a pass stopped at is the one after the last timestamp slot that
214	// came back (slot k is written after dispatch k-1).
215	func (r *recorder) dumpRange() {
216		spec := os.Getenv("LLM_DISPATCH_DUMP")
217		if spec == "" {
218			return
219		}
220		lo, hi := 0, len(r.d)
221		if a, b, ok := strings.Cut(spec, ":"); ok {
222			if v, err := strconv.Atoi(a); err == nil {
223				lo = v
224			}
225			if v, err := strconv.Atoi(b); err == nil {
226				hi = v
227			}
228		}
229		lo, hi = max(lo, 0), minInt(hi, len(r.d))
230		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "dispatch dump: %d recorded, showing %d-%d\n", len(r.d), lo, hi-1)
231		for i := lo; i < hi; i++ {
232			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "  %4d %-5s groups %dx%d pc %d\n",
233				i, r.owner[i], r.d[i].GroupsX, r.d[i].GroupsY, len(r.d[i].PushConstants))
234		}
235	}

1	// Package vk is a minimal Go wrapper around shim.c/shim.h, which does the
2	// actual Vulkan calls. See shim.h for why the struct-building work lives in
3	// C rather than here.
4	package vk
5	
6	/*
7	#cgo pkg-config: vulkan
8	#include "shim.h"
9	#include <stdlib.h>
10	*/
11	import "C"
12	
13	import (
14		"fmt"
15		"strings"
16		"time"
17		"unsafe"
18	)
19	
20	// Error wraps a non-VK_SUCCESS VkResult.
21	type Error struct {
22		Op     string
23		Result C.VkResult
24	}
25	
26	func (e *Error) Error() string {
27		return fmt.Sprintf("vk: %s failed: VkResult(%d)", e.Op, int32(e.Result))
28	}
29	
30	func check(op string, r C.VkResult) error {
31		if r != C.VK_SUCCESS {
32			return &Error{Op: op, Result: r}
33		}
34		return nil
35	}
36	
37	func boolToVk(b bool) C.VkBool32 {
38		if b {
39			return C.VK_TRUE
40		}
41		return C.VK_FALSE
42	}
43	
44	// Instance wraps a VkInstance.
45	type Instance struct {
46		handle C.VkInstance
47	}
48	
49	// NewInstance creates a VkInstance with no extensions or layers — enough for
50	// headless compute. appName is purely informational (shows up in tools like
51	// validation layers or GPU profilers).
52	func NewInstance(appName string) (*Instance, error) {
53		cAppName := C.CString(appName)
54		defer C.free(unsafe.Pointer(cAppName))
55	
56		var handle C.VkInstance
57		if err := check("vkCreateInstance", C.shim_create_instance(cAppName, &handle)); err != nil {
58			return nil, err
59		}
60		return &Instance{handle: handle}, nil
61	}

305	// Buffer is a VkBuffer bound to host-visible memory (device-local when the
306	// hardware supports it — see shim_create_storage_buffer), mapped for the
307	// lifetime of the buffer.

309		dev    *Device
310		handle C.VkBuffer
311		memory C.VkDeviceMemory
312		mapped unsafe.Pointer

316	// Memory property bits, as reported per memory type. Named here rather than
317	// imported from cgo so a caller can test them without the C types.
318	const (
319		MemoryDeviceLocal    = 0x0001
320		MemoryHostVisible    = 0x0002
321		MemoryHostCoherent   = 0x0004
322		MemoryHostCached     = 0x0008
323		MemoryDeviceCoherent = 0x0040 // VK_AMD_device_coherent_memory
324		MemoryDeviceUncached = 0x0080 // VK_AMD_device_coherent_memory
325	)

327	// MemoryType is one entry of the device's memory-type table, with the heap it
328	// draws from. This device exposes eleven of them across two heaps that overlap
329	// the same physical RAM, and which one a weight bank lands in decides both how
330	// large it may be (heap 1 stops at 83.79 GiB) and, possibly, how fast it
331	// reads — IDEAS §5.1, LLM.md L0b.
332	type MemoryType struct {
333		Index            uint32
334		HeapIndex        uint32
335		Flags            uint32
336		HeapSize         uint64
337		BufferCompatible bool // can back a plain storage buffer
338	}
339	
340	// Has reports whether every bit in want is set.
341	func (m MemoryType) Has(want uint32) bool { return m.Flags&want == want }
342	
343	// String renders the property bits the way vulkaninfo names them, shortened.
344	func (m MemoryType) String() string {
345		names := []struct {
346			bit  uint32
347			name string
348		}{
349			{MemoryDeviceLocal, "DEVICE_LOCAL"},
350			{MemoryHostVisible, "HOST_VISIBLE"},
351			{MemoryHostCoherent, "HOST_COHERENT"},
352			{MemoryHostCached, "HOST_CACHED"},
353			{MemoryDeviceCoherent, "DEVICE_COHERENT"},
354			{MemoryDeviceUncached, "DEVICE_UNCACHED"},
355		}
356		var parts []string
357		for _, n := range names {
358			if m.Flags&n.bit != 0 {
359				parts = append(parts, n.name)
360			}
361		}
362		if len(parts) == 0 {
363			return "-"
364		}
365		return strings.Join(parts, "|")
366	}

368	// MemoryTypes returns the device's memory-type table.
369	func (d *Device) MemoryTypes() ([]MemoryType, error) {
370		const max = 32
371		raw := make([]C.ShimMemoryType, max)
372		var count C.uint32_t
373		if err := check("vkGetPhysicalDeviceMemoryProperties",
374			C.shim_memory_types(d.handle, d.phys.handle, &raw[0], C.uint32_t(max), &count)); err != nil {
375			return nil, err
376		}
377		n := int(count)
378		if n > max {
379			n = max
380		}
381		out := make([]MemoryType, n)
382		for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
383			out[i] = MemoryType{
384				Index:            uint32(raw[i].index),
385				HeapIndex:        uint32(raw[i].heapIndex),
386				Flags:            uint32(raw[i].propertyFlags),
387				HeapSize:         uint64(raw[i].heapSize),
388				BufferCompatible: raw[i].bufferCompatible != 0,
389			}
390		}
391		return out, nil
392	}

394	// NewHostCachedBuffer allocates a storage buffer from a HOST_CACHED memory
395	// type when the device has one, and falls back to NewBuffer when it does not.
396	//
397	// It exists for **activation arenas the host reads back**, and the difference
398	// is not marginal. On this device the type NewBuffer prefers —
399	// DEVICE_LOCAL|HOST_VISIBLE|HOST_COHERENT, write-combined — is written at
400	// 50 GB/s and read at **0.18**, because an uncached mapping turns a read into
401	// one uncached load per cache line. A HOST_CACHED type reads the same buffer
402	// at **24.8 GB/s**, 138x, and writes it at 70. See LLM.md L6b.
403	//
404	// It is not the right choice for a weight bank: those are written once and
405	// never read, so the cached type buys only its faster write, and the GPU-side
406	// rate is what a bank is about (L0b: every type reads at 236-237 GB/s from
407	// the device, so the choice is free there and it is not free here).
408	func (d *Device) NewHostCachedBuffer(size int) (*Buffer, error) {
409		types, err := d.MemoryTypes()
410		if err != nil {
411			return nil, err
412		}
413		const want = MemoryHostVisible | MemoryHostCoherent | MemoryHostCached
414		for _, mt := range types {
415			if mt.BufferCompatible && mt.Has(want) {
416				return d.NewBufferOfType(size, mt.Index)
417			}
418		}
419		return d.NewBuffer(size)
420	}
421	
422	// NewBufferOfType allocates a storage buffer from a named memory type rather
423	// than from the one NewBuffer prefers. A type without HOST_VISIBLE cannot be
424	// mapped, so MappedPointer and every Write/Read method on the result are
425	// unusable — such a buffer is only good for a kernel that reads whatever the
426	// allocation happened to contain, which is exactly what the bandwidth probes
427	// want.
428	func (d *Device) NewBufferOfType(size int, memType uint32) (*Buffer, error) {
429		var handle C.VkBuffer
430		var memory C.VkDeviceMemory
431		var mapped unsafe.Pointer
432		if err := check("vkCreateBuffer/vkAllocateMemory",
433			C.shim_create_storage_buffer_of_type(d.handle, C.VkDeviceSize(size), C.uint32_t(memType),
434				&handle, &memory, &mapped)); err != nil {
435			return nil, err
436		}
437		return &Buffer{dev: d, handle: handle, memory: memory, mapped: mapped, size: size}, nil
438	}
439	
440	// Mapped reports whether the buffer's memory could be mapped, which is false
441	// only for a NewBufferOfType on a type without HOST_VISIBLE.
442	func (b *Buffer) Mapped() bool { return b.mapped != nil }

444	// NewBuffer allocates a buffer of size bytes usable as a storage buffer in a
445	// compute shader, left mapped.
446	func (d *Device) NewBuffer(size int) (*Buffer, error) {
447		var handle C.VkBuffer
448		var memory C.VkDeviceMemory

450		if err := check("vkCreateBuffer/vkAllocateMemory",
451			C.shim_create_storage_buffer(d.handle, d.phys.handle, C.VkDeviceSize(size), &handle, &memory, &mapped)); err != nil {
452			return nil, err
453		}
454		return &Buffer{dev: d, handle: handle, memory: memory, mapped: mapped, size: size}, nil
455	}

457	// Destroy unmaps and releases the buffer's memory and handle.

459		C.shim_destroy_buffer(b.dev.handle, b.handle, b.memory)
460	}

462	// Size returns the buffer's size in bytes.
463	func (b *Buffer) Size() int { return b.size }
464	
465	// WriteFloat32 copies src into the buffer's mapped memory starting at byte 0.
466	func (b *Buffer) WriteFloat32(src []float32) {
467		dst := unsafe.Slice((*float32)(b.mapped), len(src))
468		copy(dst, src)
469	}
470	
471	// ReadFloat32 reads n float32s back out of the buffer's mapped memory.
472	func (b *Buffer) ReadFloat32(n int) []float32 {
473		src := unsafe.Slice((*float32)(b.mapped), n)
474		out := make([]float32, n)
475		copy(out, src)
476		return out
477	}
478	
479	// WriteFloat32At copies src into the buffer's mapped memory at an element
480	// offset, so several tensors can share one arena.
481	func (b *Buffer) WriteFloat32At(off int, src []float32) {
482		dst := unsafe.Slice((*float32)(b.mapped), off+len(src))
483		copy(dst[off:], src)
484	}
485	
486	// ReadFloat32At reads n float32s starting at an element offset. Reading a
487	// whole buffer to recover a tensor near its end is the difference between
488	// copying a few megabytes and copying gigabytes, which for the VAE decoder's
489	// activation arena was 23x the GPU time of the decode itself.
490	func (b *Buffer) ReadFloat32At(off, n int) []float32 {
491		src := unsafe.Slice((*float32)(b.mapped), off+n)
492		out := make([]float32, n)
493		copy(out, src[off:])
494		return out
495	}
496	
497	// ZeroFloat32At clears n float32s at an element offset, in place in the
498	// mapped memory.
499	//
500	// It exists because `WriteFloat32At(off, make([]float32, n))` is two costs,
501	// and on a hot path the allocation is the larger one: the gated DeltaNet's
502	// recurrent state is 3.1 MB a layer and 36 layers of it are reset at the
503	// start of every prefill, so the obvious spelling was **113 MB of Go
504	// allocation a graph** — a fixed ~55 ms whatever the prompt length, which is
505	// 12% of a 128-token pass and invisible at 2048 (LLM.md L6c-3).
506	func (b *Buffer) ZeroFloat32At(off, n int) {
507		clear(unsafe.Slice((*float32)(b.mapped), off+n)[off:])
508	}
509	
510	// ZeroUint16At clears n uint16s at an element offset, for the fp16 arenas.
511	func (b *Buffer) ZeroUint16At(off, n int) {
512		clear(unsafe.Slice((*uint16)(b.mapped), off+n)[off:])
513	}
514	
515	// Zero clears the whole buffer, which is what an arena wants once at
516	// allocation: the pad columns of every A operand and the pad rows of a short
517	// run come from here, and the kernels have no bounds checks.
518	func (b *Buffer) Zero() {
519		clear(unsafe.Slice((*byte)(b.mapped), b.size))
520	}
521	
522	// WriteUint16At copies src into the buffer's mapped memory at a uint16
523	// element offset. fp16 is the matrix cores' only operand type, so a weight
524	// arena is filled through this rather than WriteFloat32At; the caller does
525	// the narrowing, because the layout it writes into is usually a transpose or
526	// a retiling of the tensor it came from.
527	func (b *Buffer) WriteUint16At(off int, src []uint16) {
528		dst := unsafe.Slice((*uint16)(b.mapped), off+len(src))
529		copy(dst[off:], src)
530	}
531	
532	// ReadUint16At reads n uint16s starting at a uint16 element offset.
533	func (b *Buffer) ReadUint16At(off, n int) []uint16 {
534		src := unsafe.Slice((*uint16)(b.mapped), off+n)
535		out := make([]uint16, n)
536		copy(out, src[off:])
537		return out
538	}
539	
540	// ReadUint32At reads n uint32s starting at a uint32 element offset. Storage
541	// buffers that hold bit-packed data rather than numbers — a mask, an index
542	// list — are read through this instead of ReadFloat32At, so that nothing goes
543	// through a float on the way.
544	func (b *Buffer) ReadUint32At(off, n int) []uint32 {
545		src := unsafe.Slice((*uint32)(b.mapped), off+n)
546		out := make([]uint32, n)
547		copy(out, src[off:])
548		return out
549	}
550	
551	// ReadUint32 reads n uint32s back out of the buffer's mapped memory.
552	func (b *Buffer) ReadUint32(n int) []uint32 {
553		src := unsafe.Slice((*uint32)(b.mapped), n)
554		out := make([]uint32, n)
555		copy(out, src)
556		return out
557	}
558	
559	// MappedPointer returns the start of the buffer's host mapping, for callers
560	// that want to fill or read it as a type the Write*/Read* helpers don't
561	// cover, or to fill a multi-hundred-MB buffer in place rather than building
562	// a host-side copy of it first.
563	func (b *Buffer) MappedPointer() unsafe.Pointer { return b.mapped }
564	
565	// WriteBytes copies src into the buffer's mapped memory starting at byte 0.
566	func (b *Buffer) WriteBytes(src []byte) {
567		dst := unsafe.Slice((*byte)(b.mapped), len(src))
568		copy(dst, src)
569	}
570	
571	// WriteBytesAt copies src into the buffer's mapped memory at a byte offset.
572	// A quantised weight bank is staged through this rather than through
573	// WriteFloat32At: its blocks are 24, 34, 144 or 176 bytes and nothing about
574	// them is a float, so the host copies the checkpoint's own bytes and the
575	// shader unpacks them (LLM.md L5b).
576	func (b *Buffer) WriteBytesAt(off int, src []byte) {
577		dst := unsafe.Slice((*byte)(b.mapped), off+len(src))
578		copy(dst[off:], src)
579	}
580	
581	// FillRepeating tiles block across the whole buffer, in place. It exists for
582	// the multi-gigabyte weight banks IDEAS §3.5 needs: a 512-expert fp16 bank is
583	// 1.8 GB, and building a host-side copy of that to hand to WriteBytes costs
584	// more than the measurement it feeds. Only the addresses matter for a timing
585	// run, so a repeating block of real values is as good as a unique one — and
586	// it must be real values, because reinterpreting whatever the allocation held
587	// as fp16 can produce infinities that change what the arithmetic costs.
588	func (b *Buffer) FillRepeating(block []byte) {
589		if len(block) == 0 {
590			return
591		}
592		dst := unsafe.Slice((*byte)(b.mapped), b.size)
593		for off := 0; off < len(dst); off += len(block) {
594			copy(dst[off:], block)
595		}
596	}
597	
598	// ReadBytes reads n bytes back out of the buffer's mapped memory.
599	func (b *Buffer) ReadBytes(n int) []byte {
600		src := unsafe.Slice((*byte)(b.mapped), n)
601		out := make([]byte, n)
602		copy(out, src)
603		return out
604	}

628	// Destroy releases the shader module.
629	func (s *ShaderModule) Destroy() {
630		C.shim_destroy_shader_module(s.dev.handle, s.handle)
631	}
632	
633	// Handle returns the raw VkShaderModule.
634	func (s *ShaderModule) Handle() C.VkShaderModule { return s.handle }
635	
636	// SpecConstant is one uint32 specialization constant, identified by the
637	// constant ID it's declared with in GLSL (`layout(constant_id = ID)`).
638	type SpecConstant struct {
639		ID    uint32
640		Value uint32
641	}
642	
643	// PipelineSpec describes the resources a ComputePipeline binds: one storage
644	// buffer per entry in Buffers (bound to bindings 0..len(Buffers)-1), an
645	// optional push-constant range, and optional specialization constants.
646	type PipelineSpec struct {
647		Buffers []*Buffer
648		// Counts, when set, groups Buffers into descriptor *arrays*: binding i
649		// holds Counts[i] consecutive buffers, and the shader declares it as
650		// `buffer B { ... } b[N]` and indexes it with a dynamically uniform
651		// expression. Its sum must be len(Buffers). Nil is the plain
652		// arrangement — one buffer per binding, in order — which is what every
653		// kernel here but one uses.
654		//
655		// It exists because `maxStorageBufferRange` on this device is 4 GiB - 4
656		// and the MoE bank is 77 GB (LLM.md L6a): the bank is one buffer a layer,
657		// bound as one array, and the layer index selects.
658		Counts           []uint32
659		PushConstantSize uint32
660		SpecConstants    []SpecConstant
661		// RequiredSubgroupSize pins the wave size the shader runs at instead of
662		// letting the driver choose (IDEAS.md §6.2). Zero keeps the default. It
663		// must be a power of two inside the device's reported
664		// [MinSubgroupSize, MaxSubgroupSize], the shader's local_size_x must be a
665		// multiple of it, and the device must have been created with
666		// DeviceFeatures.SubgroupSizeControl — otherwise pipeline creation fails.
667		RequiredSubgroupSize uint32
668	}
669	
670	// ComputePipeline is a full pipeline (descriptor set layout, pipeline,
671	// descriptor set, command buffer, fence and timestamp query pool) built
672	// from a PipelineSpec.
673	type ComputePipeline struct {
674		dev    *Device
675		handle C.ShimComputePipeline
676	}
677	
678	// NewPipeline builds a compute pipeline for shader bound according to spec.
679	func (d *Device) NewPipeline(shader *ShaderModule, spec PipelineSpec) (*ComputePipeline, error) {
680		p := &ComputePipeline{dev: d}
681	
682		bufHandles := make([]C.VkBuffer, len(spec.Buffers))
683		for i, b := range spec.Buffers {
684			bufHandles[i] = b.handle
685		}
686		var bufPtr *C.VkBuffer
687		if len(bufHandles) > 0 {
688			bufPtr = &bufHandles[0]
689		}
690	
691		var countPtr *C.uint32_t
692		var counts []C.uint32_t
693		if len(spec.Counts) > 0 {
694			total := 0
695			for _, n := range spec.Counts {
696				total += int(n)
697			}
698			if total != len(spec.Buffers) {
699				return nil, fmt.Errorf("vk: PipelineSpec.Counts sums to %d, but there are %d buffers", total, len(spec.Buffers))
700			}
701			counts = make([]C.uint32_t, len(spec.Counts))
702			for i, n := range spec.Counts {
703				counts[i] = C.uint32_t(n)
704			}
705			countPtr = &counts[0]
706		}
707	
708		var specC []C.ShimSpecConstant
709		if len(spec.SpecConstants) > 0 {
710			specC = make([]C.ShimSpecConstant, len(spec.SpecConstants))
711			for i, sc := range spec.SpecConstants {
712				specC[i] = C.ShimSpecConstant{constantID: C.uint32_t(sc.ID), value: C.uint32_t(sc.Value)}
713			}
714		}
715		var specPtr *C.ShimSpecConstant
716		if len(specC) > 0 {
717			specPtr = &specC[0]
718		}
719	
720		if err := check("vkCreateComputePipelines",
721			C.shim_create_compute_pipeline(d.handle, shader.handle, bufPtr, C.uint32_t(len(bufHandles)),
722				countPtr, C.uint32_t(len(spec.Counts)),
723				C.uint32_t(spec.PushConstantSize), specPtr, C.uint32_t(len(specC)),
724				C.uint32_t(spec.RequiredSubgroupSize),
725				C.uint32_t(d.queueFamily), &p.handle)); err != nil {
726			p.Destroy()
727			return nil, err
728		}
729		return p, nil
730	}
731	
732	// NewComputePipeline is a convenience wrapper for the common case of a
733	// single storage-buffer binding and no push constants or specialization
734	// constants.
735	func (d *Device) NewComputePipeline(shader *ShaderModule, buf *Buffer) (*ComputePipeline, error) {
736		return d.NewPipeline(shader, PipelineSpec{Buffers: []*Buffer{buf}})
737	}
738	
739	// DispatchTimed records iterations back-to-back dispatches of
740	// (groupsX,groupsY,groupsZ) workgroups (with a barrier between each, so
741	// in-place steady-state throughput is what gets measured), submits them,
742	// blocks until complete, and returns the GPU-side elapsed time measured via
743	// timestamp queries — not wall-clock time, so it excludes CPU submission and
744	// scheduling overhead.
745	func (p *ComputePipeline) DispatchTimed(groupsX, groupsY, groupsZ, iterations uint32, pushConstants []byte) (time.Duration, error) {
746		var start, end C.uint64_t
747		var pcPtr unsafe.Pointer
748		var pcLen C.uint32_t
749		if len(pushConstants) > 0 {
750			pcPtr = unsafe.Pointer(&pushConstants[0])
751			pcLen = C.uint32_t(len(pushConstants))
752		}
753		if err := check("vkQueueSubmit", C.shim_dispatch_timed(p.dev.handle, p.dev.queue, &p.handle,
754			C.uint32_t(groupsX), C.uint32_t(groupsY), C.uint32_t(groupsZ), C.uint32_t(iterations),
755			pcPtr, pcLen, &start, &end)); err != nil {
756			return 0, err
757		}
758		ticks := float64(uint64(end)) - float64(uint64(start))
759		ns := ticks * p.dev.phys.TimestampPeriod
760		return time.Duration(ns), nil
761	}
762	
763	// DispatchSequenceTimed is DispatchTimed for a sequence of dispatches that
764	// differ in their push constants: the i-th covers groupsX[i] workgroups on
765	// the X axis and pushes pushConstants[i], and a barrier separates every
766	// dispatch from the next — within one iteration and across iterations alike.
767	//
768	// It exists for IDEAS §3.5's baseline. A grouped kernel's claim is that one
769	// dispatch over a tile table beats one dispatch per expert, and the losing
770	// arm of that comparison is a sequence of 512 dispatches whose only
771	// difference is where in the table each starts. Expressing that with
772	// DispatchTimed is impossible (one constant block per command buffer), and
773	// expressing it as 512 separate submits would measure the CPU's submit path
774	// instead of the GPU's.
775	//
776	// Every element of pushConstants must be the same length, since the pipeline
777	// layout declares one range.
778	func (p *ComputePipeline) DispatchSequenceTimed(groupsX []uint32, groupsY, groupsZ, iterations uint32, pushConstants [][]byte) (time.Duration, error) {
779		if len(groupsX) == 0 {
780			return 0, fmt.Errorf("DispatchSequenceTimed: empty dispatch sequence")
781		}
782		if len(pushConstants) != 0 && len(pushConstants) != len(groupsX) {
783			return 0, fmt.Errorf("DispatchSequenceTimed: %d push-constant blocks for %d dispatches",
784				len(pushConstants), len(groupsX))
785		}
786		// Flattened into one contiguous buffer because cgo will not let a Go
787		// slice of Go slices cross the boundary.
788		var flat []byte
789		var pcSize int
790		if len(pushConstants) > 0 {
791			pcSize = len(pushConstants[0])
792			flat = make([]byte, 0, pcSize*len(pushConstants))
793			for i, b := range pushConstants {
794				if len(b) != pcSize {
795					return 0, fmt.Errorf("DispatchSequenceTimed: push-constant block %d is %d bytes, block 0 is %d",
796						i, len(b), pcSize)
797				}
798				flat = append(flat, b...)
799			}
800		}
801	
802		var start, end C.uint64_t
803		var pcPtr unsafe.Pointer
804		if len(flat) > 0 {
805			pcPtr = unsafe.Pointer(&flat[0])
806		}
807		if err := check("vkQueueSubmit", C.shim_dispatch_seq_timed(p.dev.handle, p.dev.queue, &p.handle,
808			(*C.uint32_t)(unsafe.Pointer(&groupsX[0])), C.uint32_t(len(groupsX)),
809			C.uint32_t(groupsY), C.uint32_t(groupsZ), C.uint32_t(iterations),
810			pcPtr, C.uint32_t(pcSize), &start, &end)); err != nil {
811			return 0, err
812		}
813		ticks := float64(uint64(end)) - float64(uint64(start))
814		return time.Duration(ticks * p.dev.phys.TimestampPeriod), nil
815	}
816	
817	// MultiDispatch is one dispatch of a mixed-pipeline sequence: which pipeline
818	// runs, over what grid, with which push constants.
819	type MultiDispatch struct {
820		Pipeline      *ComputePipeline
821		GroupsX       uint32
822		GroupsY       uint32
823		PushConstants []byte
824	}
825	
826	// DispatchMultiTimed is DispatchSequenceTimed for a sequence whose dispatches
827	// use *different pipelines* and *different grid extents*.
828	//
829	// It exists for the mixed-width MoE decode dispatch (IDEAS §1.12). The M block
830	// a grouped GEMV carries is compiled in, so covering a routing histogram with
831	// several widths at once is one dispatch per width, each binding the build for
832	// that width and naming its own contiguous slice of the shared slot table. The
833	// dispatches write disjoint output rows, so `barriers` is a knob rather than a
834	// requirement: false lets the widths overlap the way an engine would let them,
835	// true charges the split a compute->compute barrier between every pair, which
836	// is what it costs if the overlap cannot be had.
837	//
838	// Every pipeline must have been built over the same buffers and the same
839	// push-constant size — the recording uses the first one's command buffer,
840	// query pool and fence — and every push-constant block must be the same
841	// length, since each pipeline layout declares one range.
842	func DispatchMultiTimed(dispatches []MultiDispatch, groupsZ, iterations uint32, barriers bool) (time.Duration, error) {
843		d, _, err := dispatchMulti(dispatches, groupsZ, iterations, barriers, false)
844		return d, err
845	}
846	
847	// DispatchMultiMarked records the same sequence and returns **one duration per
848	// dispatch** as well as the total, by writing a timestamp after each rather
849	// than only at the two ends.
850	//
851	// It is what makes one command buffer a *token* affordable to reason about
852	// (LLM.md L7d). A submit and a fence wait is ~40 us on this device and a
853	// decode step was ~490 of them, one a block — so merging them is worth about
854	// 15% — but the per-block wall clock the engine has been tuned by lives in
855	// exactly those boundaries. This moves the attribution inside the command
856	// buffer, where it is GPU time rather than host time and so is strictly the
857	// better number: it is what GGML_VK_PERF_LOGGER reports for llama.cpp's own
858	// graph, on our side of the comparison.
859	//
860	// One pass only, and at most SHIM_QUERY_SLOTS-1 dispatches; past either it
861	// falls back to the total, and the per-dispatch slice comes back nil.
862	func DispatchMultiMarked(dispatches []MultiDispatch, barriers bool) (time.Duration, []time.Duration, error) {
863		return dispatchMulti(dispatches, 1, 1, barriers, true)
864	}
865	
866	func dispatchMulti(dispatches []MultiDispatch, groupsZ, iterations uint32, barriers, marks bool) (time.Duration, []time.Duration, error) {
867		if len(dispatches) == 0 {
868			return 0, nil, fmt.Errorf("DispatchMultiTimed: empty dispatch sequence")
869		}
870		dev := dispatches[0].Pipeline.dev
871		// The pipelines are copied by value rather than referenced: a
872		// ShimComputePipeline holds nothing but Vulkan handles, so a Go slice of
873		// them carries no Go pointers and can cross the cgo boundary, which a
874		// slice of *C.ShimComputePipeline could not.
875		handles := make([]C.ShimComputePipeline, len(dispatches))
876		groupsX := make([]C.uint32_t, len(dispatches))
877		groupsY := make([]C.uint32_t, len(dispatches))
878		var flat []byte
879		pcSize := len(dispatches[0].PushConstants)
880		for i, d := range dispatches {
881			if d.Pipeline == nil {
882				return 0, nil, fmt.Errorf("DispatchMultiTimed: dispatch %d has no pipeline", i)
883			}
884			if d.Pipeline.dev != dev {
885				return 0, nil, fmt.Errorf("DispatchMultiTimed: dispatch %d is on a different device", i)
886			}
887			if len(d.PushConstants) != pcSize {
888				return 0, nil, fmt.Errorf("DispatchMultiTimed: push-constant block %d is %d bytes, block 0 is %d",
889					i, len(d.PushConstants), pcSize)
890			}
891			handles[i] = d.Pipeline.handle
892			groupsX[i] = C.uint32_t(d.GroupsX)
893			groupsY[i] = C.uint32_t(d.GroupsY)
894			flat = append(flat, d.PushConstants...)
895		}
896	
897		var start, end C.uint64_t
898		var pcPtr unsafe.Pointer
899		if len(flat) > 0 {
900			pcPtr = unsafe.Pointer(&flat[0])
901		}
902		var barrierFlag C.uint32_t
903		if barriers {
904			barrierFlag = 1
905		}
906		var markBuf []C.uint64_t
907		var markPtr *C.uint64_t
908		if marks && len(dispatches)+1 <= int(C.SHIM_QUERY_SLOTS) {
909			markBuf = make([]C.uint64_t, len(dispatches)+1)
910			markPtr = &markBuf[0]
911		}
912		if err := check("dispatch sequence", C.shim_dispatch_multi_timed(dev.handle, dev.queue,
913			&handles[0],
914			&groupsX[0], &groupsY[0], C.uint32_t(len(dispatches)),
915			C.uint32_t(groupsZ), C.uint32_t(iterations), barrierFlag,
916			pcPtr, C.uint32_t(pcSize), &start, &end, markPtr)); err != nil {
917			return 0, nil, err
918		}
919		ticks := float64(uint64(end)) - float64(uint64(start))
920		total := time.Duration(ticks * dev.phys.TimestampPeriod)
921		if markBuf == nil {
922			return total, nil, nil
923		}
924		each := make([]time.Duration, len(dispatches))
925		for i := range each {
926			d := float64(uint64(markBuf[i+1])) - float64(uint64(markBuf[i]))
927			each[i] = time.Duration(d * dev.phys.TimestampPeriod)
928		}
929		return total, each, nil
930	}
931	
932	// Dispatch records and submits a single dispatch covering groupsX
933	// workgroups on the X axis, then blocks until it completes. Its GPU timing
934	// is discarded — use DispatchTimed for benchmarking.
935	func (p *ComputePipeline) Dispatch(groupsX uint32) error {
936		_, err := p.DispatchTimed(groupsX, 1, 1, 1, nil)
937		return err
938	}
939	
940	// Destroy releases every object the pipeline owns.
941	func (p *ComputePipeline) Destroy() {
942		C.shim_destroy_compute_pipeline(p.dev.handle, &p.handle)
943	}

1	<!-- LLM.md P1. Where a decode token's 30.5 ms goes, at the resolution of a
2	     dispatch label. Cited from llm/record.go, llm/graph.go, llm/model.go and
3	     cmd/llm/generate.go. -->
4	
5	[← LLM.md](../LLM.md) · [← LLM2.md](../LLM2.md) · [research index](README.md) · [P0](p0-ring-watchdog.md) · [L8d](l8d-moe-decode.md) · [L8e](l8e-attn-decode.md) · phase 2
6	
7	# P1 — the decode step, attributed: the 12 ms is three things, and one of them was disk
8	
9	**Result: the step now sums.** A decode token is **30.52 ms** and every
10	microsecond of it has a name — 36 dispatch labels, six host phases, a residual
11	of 5 us. LLM2's "~12 ms a token unexplained by bytes at any achievable rate"
12	was real and is now **12.01 ms in three parts**:
13	
14	    weight-streaming dispatches, below 227 GB/s     5.54 ms
15	    dispatches that stream no weight at all         3.46 ms
16	    the host, outside the command buffer            3.01 ms
17	                                                   -------
18	                                                   12.01 ms
19	
20	**And the measurement paid for itself before the analysis did.** The host
21	third was dominated by the PLE n-gram gather at 2.24 ms a token, which turned
22	out not to be compute: sixteen random rows of a 28.80 GB mmap'd table are
23	**16.3 major page faults a step**, served one at a time. Issuing the same
24	sixteen concurrently — identical fault count, identical bytes — is **7.0-7.5x**
25	on the micro-benchmark and takes the gather from 2.244 to 0.902 ms in the whole
26	model. **Decode goes 31.51 → 32.72 tok/s, 1.30x llama.cpp.**
27	
28	## The instrument
29	
30	Every block's `graph` method has always built a `kinds []string` beside its
31	dispatches, for its error messages. Nothing read it: `recorder.add` took the
32	*block's* name and the per-dispatch timestamps L7d already collects were folded
33	into six rows. So the block table said the MoE is 11.6 ms of the token and
34	could not say which of its nine kernels that was.
35	
36	`add` now takes the labels too, `GraphStats` carries a `map[string]DispatchStat`
37	beside the six block rows, and `-gen -attrib` prints it with the host side:
38	
39	    go run ./cmd/llm -gen -model $M -n 64 -prompt 'The capital of France is' \
40	        -attrib -csv results/p1_decode_attrib.csv
41	
42	A mark-to-mark interval is the dispatch **and** the barrier in front of it, so
43	the labels sum to the whole command buffer by construction and there is no
44	barrier residual to argue about. The host rows are wall clock around the loop's
45	own calls; `submit+fence` contains the dispatches, so the step is
46	`dispatches + (submit - GPU) + gather + record + sample + detokenize + emit`.
47	Two runs: **32.67 and 32.76 tok/s**, 0.3% apart.
48	
49	## Where the token goes
50	
51	30.52 ms a step, 1501 dispatches a pass in 2 command buffers, at the shipped
52	bank (five dense families at 4.5 bits, 4.281 GB a token). `GB/tok` is
53	`cmd/gguf -width`'s inventory for that family; `ms@227` is what those bytes
54	cost at the best dispatch rate ever measured on this machine (L8c-7's fused
55	attention projection, 39.5 MB in 174.3 us).
56	
57	| family | GB/tok | ms | GB/s | % of 242 | ms@227 | lost |
58	|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
59	| moe experts, gate+up | 1.003 | 4.998 | 200.6 | 82.9% | 4.417 | +0.58 |
60	| **moe experts, down** | 0.501 | 3.399 | **147.5** | 60.9% | 2.209 | **+1.19** |
61	| deltanet | 1.174 | 5.827 | 201.5 | 83.3% | 5.172 | +0.66 |
62	| **hyper_conn** | 0.360 | 3.142 | **114.6** | 47.3% | 1.586 | **+1.56** |
63	| lm_head | 0.358 | 1.936 | 184.9 | 76.4% | 1.577 | +0.36 |
64	| full_attn + indexer | 0.347 | 1.704 | 203.6 | 84.1% | 1.529 | +0.18 |
65	| moe_router | 0.252 | 0.764 | *329.8* | *136.3%* | 1.110 | −0.35 |
66	| **moe shared expert** | 0.251 | 1.839 | **136.5** | 56.4% | 1.106 | **+0.73** |
67	| ple_proj | 0.035 | 0.441 | 79.4 | 32.8% | 0.154 | +0.29 |
68	| **total** | **4.281** | **24.050** | **178.0** | **73.6%** | 18.859 | **+5.54** |
69	
70	`moe_router` reads above the bus, which by **D16** is not a DRAM measurement:
71	its 2.63 MB a layer never leaves the MALL (D12), so its 0.252 GB is in the
72	*inventory* and not in the traffic. It is excluded from the loss column.
73	
74	Beside those, **3.46 ms of dispatches that stream no weight at all** (11.3% of
75	the step) — the recurrence, the moves, the permutations and the norms:
76	
77	    dn.scan 0.638   hc.norm 0.610   move 0.563   hc.combine 0.359
78	    moe.route 0.285  attn.attn 0.194  moe.combine 0.160  dn.conv 0.141
79	    moe.perm.up 0.139  dn.norm 0.125  attn.score 0.114  attn.pack 0.091
80	    dn.hist 0.036  ple.conv 0.004  ple.hist 0.001
81	
82	And **3.01 ms of host** (9.9%):
83	
84	    record          1.127     building push constants for 1501 dispatches,
85	                              plus the 0.99 MB logits read-back
86	    gather (ple)    0.902     the n-gram table, below
87	    hand-over       0.828     submit + fence, minus the GPU time inside it
88	    sample          0.142     argmax over 151 936 logits
89	    detokenize      0.002
90	    emit            0.005
91	    unattributed    0.005
92	
93	## Finding 1 — the n-gram gather was disk latency, and it was serial
94	
95	`Model.PLEGather` reads sixteen rows of `per_layer_token_embd` a token: 90
96	bytes each, 1.41 KB in total, at sixteen *random* offsets into a 320-million-row,
97	**28.80 GB** mmap'd table that D2 deliberately keeps off the device. On a
98	machine holding 84 GB of resident model those rows are not in the page cache.
99	Counting `majflt` around 200 gathers of fresh random rows:
100	
101	| arm | us a step | minflt a step | **majflt a step** |
102	|---|---:|---:|---:|
103	| serial (as written) | 853.2 / 819.4 | 0.6 / 0.1 | 16.27 / 16.29 |
104	| sixteen touched concurrently, then gathered | **122.2 / 108.8** | 0.3 / 0.1 | 16.34 / 16.30 |
105	
106	**The fault count is identical to two decimal places.** Nothing is read that
107	was not read before, no readahead is re-enabled, no page is cached that was not
108	cached. What changes is that sixteen faults are outstanding at once instead of
109	one at a time — 7.0-7.5x, and the whole of it is device latency.
110	
111	So the gather goes parallel: a bounded worker pool over the rows, destinations
112	disjoint, one scratch buffer a worker. Value for value it is the same function.
