# P1 — the decode step, attributed: the 12 ms is three things, and one of them was disk

**Result: the step now sums.** A decode token is **30.52 ms** and every
microsecond of it has a name — 36 dispatch labels, six host phases, a residual
of 5 us. LLM2's "~12 ms a token unexplained by bytes at any achievable rate"
was real and is now **12.01 ms in three parts**:

    weight-streaming dispatches, below 227 GB/s     5.54 ms
    dispatches that stream no weight at all         3.46 ms
    the host, outside the command buffer            3.01 ms
                                                   -------
                                                   12.01 ms

**And the measurement paid for itself before the analysis did.** The host
third was dominated by the PLE n-gram gather at 2.24 ms a token, which turned
out not to be compute: sixteen random rows of a 28.80 GB mmap'd table are
**16.3 major page faults a step**, served one at a time. Issuing the same
sixteen concurrently — identical fault count, identical bytes — is **7.0-7.5x**
on the micro-benchmark and takes the gather from 2.244 to 0.902 ms in the whole
model. **Decode goes 31.51 → 32.72 tok/s, 1.30x llama.cpp.**

## The instrument

Every block's `graph` method has always built a `kinds []string` beside its
dispatches, for its error messages. Nothing read it: `recorder.add` took the
*block's* name and the per-dispatch timestamps L7d already collects were folded
into six rows. So the block table said the MoE is 11.6 ms of the token and
could not say which of its nine kernels that was.

`add` now takes the labels too, `GraphStats` carries a `map[string]DispatchStat`
beside the six block rows, and `-gen -attrib` prints it with the host side:

    go run ./cmd/llm -gen -model $M -n 64 -prompt 'The capital of France is' \
        -attrib -csv results/p1_decode_attrib.csv

A mark-to-mark interval is the dispatch **and** the barrier in front of it, so
the labels sum to the whole command buffer by construction and there is no
barrier residual to argue about. The host rows are wall clock around the loop's
own calls; `submit+fence` contains the dispatches, so the step is
`dispatches + (submit - GPU) + gather + record + sample + detokenize + emit`.
Two runs: **32.67 and 32.76 tok/s**, 0.3% apart.

## Where the token goes

30.52 ms a step, 1501 dispatches a pass in 2 command buffers, at the shipped
bank (five dense families at 4.5 bits, 4.281 GB a token). `GB/tok` is
`cmd/gguf -width`'s inventory for that family; `ms@227` is what those bytes
cost at the best dispatch rate ever measured on this machine (L8c-7's fused
attention projection, 39.5 MB in 174.3 us).

| family | GB/tok | ms | GB/s | % of 242 | ms@227 | lost |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| moe experts, gate+up | 1.003 | 4.998 | 200.6 | 82.9% | 4.417 | +0.58 |
| **moe experts, down** | 0.501 | 3.399 | **147.5** | 60.9% | 2.209 | **+1.19** |
| deltanet | 1.174 | 5.827 | 201.5 | 83.3% | 5.172 | +0.66 |
| **hyper_conn** | 0.360 | 3.142 | **114.6** | 47.3% | 1.586 | **+1.56** |
| lm_head | 0.358 | 1.936 | 184.9 | 76.4% | 1.577 | +0.36 |
| full_attn + indexer | 0.347 | 1.704 | 203.6 | 84.1% | 1.529 | +0.18 |
| moe_router | 0.252 | 0.764 | *329.8* | *136.3%* | 1.110 | −0.35 |
| **moe shared expert** | 0.251 | 1.839 | **136.5** | 56.4% | 1.106 | **+0.73** |
| ple_proj | 0.035 | 0.441 | 79.4 | 32.8% | 0.154 | +0.29 |
| **total** | **4.281** | **24.050** | **178.0** | **73.6%** | 18.859 | **+5.54** |

`moe_router` reads above the bus, which by **D16** is not a DRAM measurement:
its 2.63 MB a layer never leaves the MALL (D12), so its 0.252 GB is in the
*inventory* and not in the traffic. It is excluded from the loss column.

Beside those, **3.46 ms of dispatches that stream no weight at all** (11.3% of
the step) — the recurrence, the moves, the permutations and the norms:

    dn.scan 0.638   hc.norm 0.610   move 0.563   hc.combine 0.359
    moe.route 0.285  attn.attn 0.194  moe.combine 0.160  dn.conv 0.141
    moe.perm.up 0.139  dn.norm 0.125  attn.score 0.114  attn.pack 0.091
    dn.hist 0.036  ple.conv 0.004  ple.hist 0.001

And **3.01 ms of host** (9.9%):

    record          1.127     building push constants for 1501 dispatches,
                              plus the 0.99 MB logits read-back
    gather (ple)    0.902     the n-gram table, below
    hand-over       0.828     submit + fence, minus the GPU time inside it
    sample          0.142     argmax over 151 936 logits
    detokenize      0.002
    emit            0.005
    unattributed    0.005

| arm | us a step | minflt a step | **majflt a step** |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| serial (as written) | 853.2 / 819.4 | 0.6 / 0.1 | 16.27 / 16.29 |

## Finding 3 — the MoE's down projection is 1.19 ms behind its own up

## Finding 4 — record + hand-over is 1.96 ms, and now it is priced

1	package llm
2	
3	// The graph (LLM.md L6b): the five blocks in llama.cpp's own order, over one
4	// resident model, from a token list to logits.
5	//
6	// L6a put every weight on the device — 84.20 GB in 68 buffers — but nothing
7	// had ever run two blocks in sequence. Each of them was built against the
8	// oracle in isolation: llama.cpp's own value for the tensor it reads went in,
9	// and its value for the tensor it writes came out. This file is where the
10	// inputs stop being the reference's and start being ours, which is the only
11	// way the thing that has been built since L2 is a model rather than five
12	// kernels.
13	//
14	// The order is `llama_model_qwen4exp::graph::graph`, and it is not the
15	// obvious one:
16	//
17	//	res = repeat(embed(ids), hc)            "hc_init"
18	//	for each layer:
19	//	    if it is the PLE layer: res += ple(res, ngram_embd)
20	//	    mixed, inject = hc_mix(res, attn)   the layer's *attention* mixer
21	//	    out = deltanet(mixed) | attention(mixed)
22	//	    res = hc_combine(res, out, inject)  "hc_combine-L"
23	//	    mixed, inject = hc_mix(res, ffn)
24	//	    out = moe(mixed)                    "ffn_out-L"
25	//	    res = hc_combine(res, out, inject)  "l_last-L"
26	//	norm = hc_mix(res[last], head)          "result_norm" -- there is no
27	//	logits = output * norm                  separate output norm
28	//
29	// Two things about that are worth saying out loud. The final mixer and the
30	// head run on **one row**: llama.cpp's `inp_out_ids` drops every token but
31	// the last before them, and the trace agrees — `result_output` is one row of
32	// 248320 floats for a seven-token prompt. And the residual never leaves the
33	// hyper-connection block's arena: `llm_hc_combine.comp` updates it in place,
34	// so what crosses a block boundary here is the 2560-wide `hc_mixed` going
35	// out and the 2560-wide block output coming back, not the 10240-wide stream.
36	//
37	// **The glue is a host round trip, and this is the first cut.** Every block
38	// owns its own arenas, so `hc_mixed` is read out of one fp32 arena, narrowed
39	// to halves and written into another — on this machine that is a memcpy
40	// between two mapped pointers of the same physical RAM, but it is a memcpy
41	// the reference does not do. L6b measures it rather than hiding it; fusing it
42	// away is a shared-arena change to five files and belongs to whatever comes
43	// after the number.
44	
45	import (
46		"fmt"
47		"os"
48		"runtime"
49		"runtime/debug"
50		"time"
51	
52		"strix-halo-vulkan/vk"
53	)
54	
55	// GraphOpts are the choices that change what the graph allocates.
56	type GraphOpts struct {
57		// MaxTokens is the longest prompt the arenas hold. Every block is sized
58		// for it, and the MoE block's 0.87 GB of arenas scale with it.
59		MaxTokens int
60		// NKV is the attention cache's cell count. Zero takes the reference's
61		// own rounding, MaxTokens up to 256 cells, which is what the 7-token
62		// trace was dumped at.
63		NKV int
64		// Layers truncates the model to its first N layers. It is not a model —
65		// the last mixer and the head still run — but it is how a graph gets
66		// staged in seconds instead of 33 of them while the order is being
67		// checked, and how a block's contribution is isolated by leaving the
68		// ones after it out.
69		Layers int
70		// NoHead leaves `output.weight` unstaged, which saves 1.27 GB and 20
71		// seconds for a caller that wants `result_norm` and not logits.
72		NoHead bool
73		// HeadRows is how many rows of logits the head's arena holds. One is
74		// what the reference computes and what every caller before L8c wanted:
75		// llama.cpp's graph ends with `inp_out_ids`, so prefill projects the
76		// last token alone. A perplexity run wants every row, and a row is
77		// 0.99 MB of f32 — 2.03 GB for a 2048-token chunk — so it names the
78		// slab it works in here rather than asking for the batch.
79		HeadRows int
80		// DenseFP16 stages the dense weights as halves, which is what every
81		// block did before L8. It is the control, not the default: the bank L8
82		// stages is the checkpoint's own int8 with an fp16 scale per 32 elements,
83		// which is half the bytes and — for a Q8_0 tensor — the same numbers
84		// (bank.go). `LLM_DENSE_FP16=1` sets it from the environment, on the
85		// precedent of L6b's `LLM_ARENA_UNCACHED`.
86		DenseFP16 bool
87	}
88	
89	// denseQ8 is whether the dense banks are L8's. The environment wins, so that
90	// a run can be repeated on the old bank without rebuilding a caller.
91	func (o GraphOpts) denseQ8() bool { return !o.DenseFP16 && DenseQ8() }
92	
93	// DenseQ8 is that choice for a caller with no options of its own — the block
94	// benchmarks and `-resident`. L8's bank is the default and `LLM_DENSE_FP16=1`
95	// is the control, on the precedent of L6b's `LLM_ARENA_UNCACHED`.
96	//
97	// **A width simulation forces the fp16 arm** (sim.go). L8a's int8 bank is an
98	// identity only for a Q8_0 tensor, so staging a simulated Q4 weight through
99	// it would quantise twice and the number measured would be neither format's.
100	// The fp16 tiling holds the candidate's own halves exactly, which is the
101	// whole basis of the simulation, so it is the arm a sim has to use — at the
102	// cost of residency and tok/s being the fp16 arm's, which a sim cannot
103	// measure anyway.
104	func DenseQ8() bool { return os.Getenv("LLM_DENSE_FP16") != "1" && DensePlan().Off() }
105	
106	// HCFuse is whether P1a's combine+norm fusion is in use: one dispatch per
107	// mixer boundary (`llm_hc_cn.comp`) instead of a scatter and a norm.
108	// `LLM_HC_NOFUSE=1` puts the pair back, which is the control the write-up's
109	// numbers are measured against and the arm
110	// TestHCFusionIsTheCombineThenTheNorm compares against.
111	//
112	// The two arms compute the **same bits**, which is what makes the control
113	// worth keeping: the combine is elementwise and the fused kernel keeps the
114	// norm's 256-thread partition and its 256-way tree, so nothing about the
115	// order of a sum changes. What changes is 94 dispatches a pass and one read
116	// of the wide residual per boundary.
117	func HCFuse() bool { return os.Getenv("LLM_HC_NOFUSE") != "1" }
118	
119	// DecodeGEMV is whether the one-token kernels L8d added are in use: the MoE's
120	// expert GEMVs and split-K router, and the dense split-K GEMV under the gated
121	// DeltaNet's two projections. They are the default; `LLM_DECODE_GEMM=1` puts
122	// every one of them back on the cooperative-matrix GEMM that ran before L8d,
123	// which is the control the write-up's numbers are measured against — and the
124	// only way to run the two side by side over one prompt, since a block chooses
125	// its rung from the batch and not from a flag at the call site.
126	//
127	// The two paths do not compute the same numbers, and the difference is the
128	// order of a sum rather than the weights: a cooperative-matrix accumulator
129	// adds sixteen k an instruction in an order the extension does not define,
130	// where a GEMV lane adds them serially and a split-K reduce adds the slabs
131	// afterwards. It is f32 round-off over a 2560-long chain — rms 1.7e-05 on a
132	// projection whose scale is 31.5 — and at temperature zero over a hundred
133	// tokens it is enough to re-word a sentence. See L8d's gate.
134	func DecodeGEMV() bool { return os.Getenv("LLM_DECODE_GEMM") != "1" }

152		attn *AttnGPU
153		moe  *MoEGPU

165		// The sequence, which is what L7 added. `past` is how many tokens of it
166		// are already behind the graph — cells in the attention cache, positions
167		// behind the PLE convolution, and tokens folded into every DeltaNet
168		// layer's recurrent state — and `ids` is the whole of it, because the
169		// n-gram gather is a trigram and a continuing run's first token still has
170		// two predecessors.

181		// rec is the pass being recorded, installed on every block for the
182		// duration of one forward pass and torn down by `flush` (record.go). It
183		// is what makes a pass **one command buffer** rather than ~490: the
184		// blocks' Run methods append to it instead of submitting.

188	// record installs the recorder on every block, so that everything from here
189	// to the matching `flush` is recorded rather than submitted. It is idempotent
190	// per pass and paired with `flush` on every return path, which is why the
191	// callers are the three entry points and not the layer loop.
192	func (g *Graph) record(rows int) {
193		if g.rec == nil {
194			g.rec = &recorder{}
195		}
196		g.rec.rows = rows
197		g.hc.rec = g.rec
198		g.move.rec = g.rec
199		if g.ple != nil {
200			g.ple.rec = g.rec
201		}
202		if g.dn != nil {
203			g.dn.rec = g.rec
204		}
205		if g.attn != nil {
206			g.attn.rec = g.rec
207		}
208		if g.moe != nil {
209			g.moe.rec = g.rec
210		}
211		if g.head != nil {
212			g.head.rec = g.rec
213		}
214	}

216	// flush submits everything recorded and folds the GPU time each block's
217	// dispatches took into Stats. Every block goes back to submitting for itself
218	// afterwards, because the per-block benchmarks and the tests drive them
219	// directly and must not depend on a graph having been here.
220	//
221	// Nothing may read a device arena between `record` and here: the dispatches
222	// have not run. That is the one rule this arrangement adds, and the three
223	// entry points below are written around it — every `Mixed()`, `Logits()` and
224	// `Res()` is after the flush.
225	func (g *Graph) flush() error {
226		if g.rec == nil {
227			return nil
228		}
229		n := g.rec.len()
230		t0 := time.Now()
231		byOwner, byKind, total, err := g.rec.submit()
232		submit := time.Since(t0)
233		g.rec = nil
234		g.hc.rec, g.move.rec = nil, nil
235		if g.ple != nil {
236			g.ple.rec = nil
237		}
238		if g.dn != nil {
239			g.dn.rec = nil
240		}
241		if g.attn != nil {
242			g.attn.rec = nil
243		}
244		if g.moe != nil {
245			g.moe.rec = nil
246		}
247		if g.head != nil {
248			g.head.rec = nil
249		}
250		if err != nil {
251			return err
252		}
253		g.Stats.Dispatches += n
254		g.Stats.GPU += total
255		g.Stats.Submit += submit
256		if g.Stats.Kinds == nil {
257			g.Stats.Kinds = make(map[string]DispatchStat, len(byKind))
258		}
259		for k, v := range byKind {
260			s := g.Stats.Kinds[k]
261			s.Count, s.GPU = s.Count+v.Count, s.GPU+v.GPU
262			g.Stats.Kinds[k] = s
263		}
264		g.Stats.HC += byOwner[ownHC]
265		g.Stats.PLE += byOwner[ownPLE]
266		g.Stats.DeltaNet += byOwner[ownDN]
267		g.Stats.Attn += byOwner[ownAttn]
268		g.Stats.MoE += byOwner[ownMoE]
269		g.Stats.Head += byOwner[ownHead]
270		g.Stats.Move += byOwner[ownMove]
271		return nil
272	}

274	// PinSchedule fixes the hyper-connection block's kernel choice so that the
275	// graph runs the same arithmetic whatever the chunk length, and puts it back
276	// on the measured schedule when off.
277	//
278	// It exists for one equality and it is the equality L7b is about. Every rung
279	// of every ladder in this vertical used to be **bit-exact** against its
280	// siblings — they change how the work is tiled and never how a sum is
281	// associated — so "a prompt in chunks is the prompt whole" could be asserted
282	// to the last place even though a one-token chunk plans different kernels
283	// than a 128-token one. L7d's split-K GEMV is the first rung that is not:
284	// dividing a 10240-long dot product 160 ways and adding the pieces back is a
285	// different association of the same products, and at one token it is the rung
286	// the schedule picks. So the exactness claim is now conditional on the
287	// schedule, and this is what lets a test say which half it is testing.
288	// **L8d widened it.** The one-token kernels that stage replaces — the MoE's
289	// expert GEMVs, its split-K router and the split-K GEMV under the DeltaNet's
290	// two projections — are not bit-exact against the GEMMs they replace either,
291	// and for the same reason: a cooperative-matrix accumulator sums sixteen k an
292	// instruction in an order the extension does not define, a GEMV lane sums them
293	// serially, and a split-K reduce adds the slabs afterwards. So the pin now
294	// covers four blocks rather than one — **five with L8e**, which puts the
295	// full-attention layer's two projections on the same kernel.
296	func (g *Graph) PinSchedule(on bool) error {
297		if g.moe != nil {
298			g.moe.PinGemv(on)
299		}
300		if g.dn != nil {
301			g.dn.PinGemv(on)
302		}
303		if g.attn != nil {
304			g.attn.PinGemv(on)
305		}
306		if !on {
307			g.hc.AutoPlan()
308			return nil
309		}
310		return g.hc.SetPlan(HCDownM1, HCUpM4)
311	}
312	
313	// ResetStats clears the accumulated timings.
314	func (g *Graph) ResetStats() { g.Stats = GraphStats{} }
315	
316	// since adds the elapsed time to one of the stat fields and returns now, so a
317	// sequence of phases is a chain of one-line calls rather than a pile of
318	// start/stop pairs.
319	// blk routes a host interval to a block's stat field — except while a pass is
320	// being recorded, when the host is only building push constants and the
321	// block's real cost comes back from the GPU marks (record.go). Then the
322	// interval is what recording it cost, which is glue.
323	func (g *Graph) blk(dst *time.Duration, t0 time.Time) time.Time {
324		if g.rec != nil {
325			return since(&g.Stats.Glue, t0)
326		}
327		return since(dst, t0)
328	}
329	
330	func since(dst *time.Duration, t0 time.Time) time.Time {
331		now := time.Now()
332		*dst += now.Sub(t0)
333		return now
334	}
335	
336	// GraphStats is where a prefill's wall clock went.
337	//
338	// The split that matters here is **block against glue**. Every block in this
339	// vertical owns its own arenas, so `hc_mixed` leaves one fp32 arena, is
340	// narrowed to halves on the host and is written into another — a memcpy
341	// between two mapped pointers of the same physical RAM on this machine, but
342	// one llama.cpp does not do. 96 of those a graph, each 2560 wide, plus the
343	// block outputs coming back. Fusing them away is a shared-arena change to
344	// five files; L6b's job is to say what they cost, not to hide them.
345	type GraphStats struct {
346		Total time.Duration
347		// Per block, the wall clock around its dispatches.
348		HC, PLE, DeltaNet, Attn, MoE, Head time.Duration
349		// The host side: the two gathers, and whatever still crosses a block
350		// boundary through host memory.
351		Gather, Glue time.Duration
352		// Move is the arena-to-arena moves, on the device (L6c).
353		Move time.Duration
354		// Runs is how many prefills these totals cover.
355		Runs int
356		// GPU is what the pass's one command buffer took end to end, and
357		// Dispatches how many dispatches went into it (L7d). The per-block rows
358		// above are GPU time inside it and so sum to a little less than GPU
359		// itself — the difference is what the barriers between dispatches cost.
360		GPU        time.Duration
361		Dispatches int
362		// Submit is the **host** wall clock around the submit and the fence
363		// wait — GPU is the part of it the timestamps saw, so `Submit - GPU` is
364		// what handing one command buffer over costs (P1). It is separated from
365		// the rest of the host side because it is the one interval a
366		// pre-recorded command buffer would not remove.
367		Submit time.Duration
368		// Kinds is the same GPU time split by each dispatch's own label rather
369		// than by the block it came from (P1). A decode step is ~490 dispatches
370		// over about thirty distinct labels, so this is the resolution at which
371		// "where does the token go" has an answer.
372		Kinds map[string]DispatchStat
373	}
374	
375	// Blocks is the time inside the five blocks and the head.
376	func (s GraphStats) Blocks() time.Duration {
377		return s.HC + s.PLE + s.DeltaNet + s.Attn + s.MoE + s.Head
378	}

380	// StagedBlock is one row of the staging plan.
381	type StagedBlock struct {
382		Name    string
383		Layers  int
384		Buffers int
385		Weights int
386		Arenas  int
387		Elapsed time.Duration
388	}
389	
390	// NewGraph stages the whole model and builds the order.
391	//
392	// The staging order is L6a-5's and for L6a-5's reason: the dense blocks are
393	// dequantised to f32 on the host on the way to the device, and the 36
394	// DeltaNet layers are 8.35 GB of transient floats at once, so they go first
395	// and their host copies are dropped between them. The 77 GB expert bank needs
396	// no host floats at all and goes last, which makes the peak the resident
397	// model rather than the resident model plus a dequantisation.
398	func NewGraph(dev *vk.Device, m *Model, opts GraphOpts) (*Graph, error) {
399		c := m.Config
400		if opts.MaxTokens <= 0 {
401			return nil, fmt.Errorf("llm: graph MaxTokens is %d", opts.MaxTokens)
402		}
403		nLayer := c.NLayer
404		if opts.Layers > 0 && opts.Layers < nLayer {
405			nLayer = opts.Layers
406		}
407		nKV := opts.NKV
408		if nKV < roundUpInt(opts.MaxTokens, 256) {
409			nKV = roundUpInt(opts.MaxTokens, 256)
410		}
411		g := &Graph{m: m, cfg: c, nLayer: nLayer, maxTok: opts.MaxTokens, nKV: nKV}
412	
413		if err := g.stage(dev, opts); err != nil {
414			g.Destroy()
415			return nil, err
416		}
417		return g, nil
418	}
419	
420	// stage puts every block on the device, in the order that keeps the peak down.
421	func (g *Graph) stage(dev *vk.Device, opts GraphOpts) error {
422		m, c := g.m, g.cfg
423		var err error
424		if g.move, err = newMover(dev); err != nil {
425			return err
426		}
427		mark := func(name string, layers, buffers, weights, arenas int, start time.Time) {
428			g.Staged = append(g.Staged, StagedBlock{name, layers, buffers, weights, arenas, time.Since(start)})
429		}
430	
431		// 1. The mixers: two a layer and the head's. Indexed 2L (attn), 2L+1
432		//    (ffn), and 2*nLayer for the head — which is why the head is staged
433		//    with them and not as a block of its own.
434		start := time.Now()
435		var mixers []HCWeights
436		for l := 0; l < g.nLayer; l++ {
437			for _, side := range []string{"attn", "ffn"} {
438				w, err := m.HCWeights(l, side)
439				if err != nil {
440					return fmt.Errorf("llm: hc layer %d %s: %w", l, side, err)
441				}
442				mixers = append(mixers, w)
443			}
444		}
445		head, err2 := m.HCWeights(-1, "")
446		if err2 != nil {
447			return fmt.Errorf("llm: hc head mixer: %w", err2)
448		}
449		mixers = append(mixers, head)
450		// L8c-6's bank, where the plan names this family. `hc_attn_down` is the
451		// tensor `simFamily` maps to "hyper_conn" and the checkpoint ships it as
452		// Q8_0, which is what the `true` says; `inject` is F32 and stays in the
453		// fp16 tail whatever this is (D13).
454		hcOpts := HCBankOpts()
455		hcOpts.Q8 = opts.denseQ8()
456		if g.hc, err = NewHCGPU(dev, c.HCConfig(), g.maxTok, mixers, hcOpts); err != nil {
457			return fmt.Errorf("llm: hc: %w", err)
458		}
459		mark("hyper-conn", len(mixers), g.hc.Buffers(), g.hc.WeightBytes(), g.hc.ActivationBytes(), start)
460		mixers = nil
461		freeHost()
462	
463		// 2. The PLE n-gram block, if this checkpoint has one. It is a single
464		//    layer — layer 1 — and the 28.80 GB table it gathers from stays
465		//    mmap'd (D2).
466		pleCfg, ok, err := m.PLEConfig()
467		if err != nil {
468			return fmt.Errorf("llm: ple config: %w", err)
469		}
470		if ok && pleRuns(pleCfg, g.nLayer) {
471			start = time.Now()
472			w, err := m.PLEWeights(pleCfg.Layers[0])
473			if err != nil {
474				return fmt.Errorf("llm: ple layer %d: %w", pleCfg.Layers[0], err)
475			}
476			if g.ple, err = NewPLEGPU(dev, pleCfg, g.maxTok, w, PLEOpts{}); err != nil {
477				return fmt.Errorf("llm: ple: %w", err)
478			}
479			g.pleCfg, g.hasPLE = pleCfg, true
480			mark("ple n-gram", len(pleCfg.Layers), g.ple.Buffers(), g.ple.WeightBytes(), g.ple.ActivationBytes(), start)
481			freeHost()
482		}
483	
484		// 3 and 4. The two kinds of attention half, and the map from a layer to
485		//    which of them it is. The interval is four, so 36 layers are the
486		//    gated DeltaNet and 12 are full attention with the QSA indexer.
487		g.kinds = make([]blockKind, g.nLayer)
488		start = time.Now()
489		var dnCfg DeltaNetConfig
490		var dns []DeltaNetWeights
491		for l := 0; l < g.nLayer; l++ {
492			cfg, ok, err := m.DeltaNetConfig(l)
493			if err != nil {
494				return fmt.Errorf("llm: deltanet config %d: %w", l, err)
495			}
496			if !ok {
497				continue
498			}
499			w, err := m.DeltaNetWeights(l)
500			if err != nil {
501				return fmt.Errorf("llm: deltanet layer %d: %w", l, err)
502			}
503			g.kinds[l] = blockKind{attn: false, idx: len(dns)}
504			dnCfg, dns = cfg, append(dns, w)
505		}
506		if len(dns) > 0 {
507			// L8c-5's bank, where the plan names this family. `attn_qkv` is the
508			// tensor `simFamily` maps to "deltanet" and the checkpoint ships it
509			// as Q8_0, which is what the `true` says — the block's own two F32
510			// matrices stay in the fp16 tail whatever this is (D13).
511			dnBank, dnSim := bankOf(opts.denseQ8()), QuantSim{}
512			if q, ok := DenseBankPlan().For("blk.0.attn_qkv.weight", true); ok {
513				dnBank, dnSim = BankQ4K, q
514			}
515			if g.dn, err = NewDeltaNetGPUBank(dev, dnCfg, g.maxTok, dns, dnBank, dnSim); err != nil {
516				return fmt.Errorf("llm: deltanet: %w", err)
517			}
518			mark("deltanet", len(dns), g.dn.Buffers(), g.dn.WeightBytes(), g.dn.ActivationBytes(), start)
519		}
520		dns = nil
521		freeHost()
522	
523		start = time.Now()
524		var atCfg AttnConfig
525		var ats []AttnWeights
526		for l := 0; l < g.nLayer; l++ {
527			cfg, ok, err := m.AttnConfig(l)
528			if err != nil {
529				return fmt.Errorf("llm: attn config %d: %w", l, err)
530			}
531			if !ok {
532				continue
533			}
534			w, err := m.AttnWeights(l)
535			if err != nil {
536				return fmt.Errorf("llm: attn layer %d: %w", l, err)
537			}
538			g.kinds[l] = blockKind{attn: true, idx: len(ats)}
539			atCfg, ats = cfg, append(ats, w)
540		}
541		if len(ats) > 0 {
542			// L8c-7's bank, where the plan names this family. `attn_q` is the
543			// tensor `simFamily` maps to "full_attn" and the checkpoint ships it
544			// as Q8_0, which is what the `true` says; the indexer's two are
545			// **BF16**, which is what the `false` says, and they are a family of
546			// their own because L4b-4 measured the score sensitive to them.
547			atBank, atSim := bankOf(opts.denseQ8()), QuantSim{}
548			if q, ok := DenseBankPlan().For("blk.0.attn_q.weight", true); ok {
549				atBank, atSim = BankQ4K, q
550			}
551			idxQ := false
552			if q, ok := DenseBankPlan().For("blk.0.indexer.q_proj.weight", false); ok {
553				if atBank != BankQ4K {
554					return fmt.Errorf("llm: qsa_indexer is staged in the fused projection's plane, so it needs full_attn on the same bank")
555				}
556				if q != atSim {
557					return fmt.Errorf("llm: full_attn is %s and qsa_indexer is %s, and they share one plane", atSim, q)
558				}
559				idxQ = true
560			}
561			if g.attn, err = NewAttnGPUBank(dev, atCfg, g.maxTok, g.nKV, ats, atBank, atSim, idxQ); err != nil {
562				return fmt.Errorf("llm: attn: %w", err)
563			}
564			mark("attention", len(ats), g.attn.Buffers(), g.attn.WeightBytes(), g.attn.ActivationBytes(), start)
565		}
566		ats = nil
567		freeHost()
568	
569		// 5. The head, before the 77 GB rather than after it: it is 2.54 GB of
570		//    host floats in flight a slab at a time, and the bank it fills is the
571		//    last dense allocation there is.
572		if !opts.NoHead {
573			start = time.Now()
574			t, err := m.Set.Get("output.weight")
575			if err != nil {
576				return fmt.Errorf("llm: output.weight: %w", err)
577			}
578			headRows := opts.HeadRows
579			if headRows <= 0 {
580				headRows = 1
581			}
582			// L8c-4's bank, where the plan names this family. Everything else
583			// is still the checkpoint's own width (D13): the 4.5-bit bank has a
584			// kernel for a matrix whose k is a multiple of 256, which is every
585			// dense weight here but the 320-wide hyper-connection pair.
586			// `true` is "the checkpoint ships it as Q8_0", which `output.weight`
587			// does — it is what `LLM_DENSE_BANK_SRC` would select on if this
588			// plan ever grew one.
589			bank, sim := bankOf(opts.denseQ8()), QuantSim{}
590			if q, ok := DenseBankPlan().For(t.Name, true); ok {
591				bank, sim = BankQ4K, q
592			}
593			if g.head, err = NewHeadGPUBank(dev, c.NEmbd, t, headRows, bank, sim); err != nil {
594				return fmt.Errorf("llm: head: %w", err)
595			}
596			mark("lm head", 1, g.head.Buffers(), g.head.WeightBytes(), g.head.ActivationBytes(), start)
597			freeHost()
598		}
599	
600		// 6. The expert banks: 97% of the parameters, staged byte for byte out
601		//    of the mmap'd checkpoint, one buffer a layer.
602		start = time.Now()
603		var moes []MoEWeights
604		for l := 0; l < g.nLayer; l++ {
605			w, err := m.MoEWeights(l)
606			if err != nil {
607				return fmt.Errorf("llm: moe layer %d: %w", l, err)
608			}
609			moes = append(moes, w)
610		}
611		if g.moe, err = NewMoEGPU(dev, m.MoEConfig(), g.maxTok, moes); err != nil {
612			return fmt.Errorf("llm: moe: %w", err)
613		}
614		mark("moe", len(moes), g.moe.Buffers(), g.moe.WeightBytes(), g.moe.ActivationBytes(), start)
615		moes = nil
616		freeHost()
617		return nil
618	}

620	// Layers is how many layers this graph runs, NKV its cache, MaxTokens its

635	// Reset starts a fresh sequence: the attention cache from cell zero, the PLE
636	// convolution from position zero, and every DeltaNet layer's recurrent state
637	// and window cleared (L7b).
638	//
639	// Only the DeltaNet's state is actually written. The other two are *masked*
640	// rather than cleared — a cell past the end of the sequence is excluded from
641	// every score, a convolution tap before position zero contributes nothing —
642	// so clearing them would be work that changes no output.
643	func (g *Graph) Reset() error {
644		g.past = 0
645		g.ids = g.ids[:0]
646		if g.attn != nil {
647			g.attn.Reset()
648		}
649		if g.ple != nil {
650			g.ple.Reset()
651		}
652		if g.dn != nil {
653			for l := 0; l < g.nLayer; l++ {
654				if k := g.kinds[l]; !k.attn {
655					if err := g.dn.Reset(k.idx); err != nil {
656						return err
657					}
658				}
659			}
660		}
661		return nil
662	}

664	// Forward runs the whole model over a prompt **as a fresh sequence** and
665	// returns the logits of its last token, which is the only row llama.cpp
666	// computes at prefill.
667	//
668	// It also returns `result_norm` — the final mixer's output, the tensor the
669	// head reads — because a logit disagreement has exactly two places to be and
670	// the caller should not have to run the graph twice to find out which.
671	func (g *Graph) Forward(ids []int32) (logits, norm []float32, err error) {
672		if err := g.Reset(); err != nil {
673			return nil, nil, err
674		}
675		return g.Extend(ids)
676	}
677	
678	// Extend runs the model over the next tokens of the sequence the graph is
679	// already holding, and returns the last one's logits.
680	//
681	// It is Forward without the reset, and it is the whole of decode: a prompt is
682	// one call with many tokens, a generated token is a call with one. What makes
683	// the two the same computation is L7a's cache and L7b's two carried
684	// histories, and what asserts it is TestGraphIsAChunkSplit.
685	func (g *Graph) Extend(ids []int32) (logits, norm []float32, err error) {
686		if g.head == nil {
687			return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("llm: this graph was staged without a head")
688		}
689		// One command buffer for the whole of it, head included (L7d): the
690		// layers, the head mixer and the projection are recorded and submitted
691		// once, and the two read-backs below are after the flush because nothing
692		// has run until then.
693		g.record(len(ids))
694		defer func() {
695			if ferr := g.flush(); ferr != nil && err == nil {
696				logits, norm, err = nil, nil, ferr
697			}
698		}()
699		if err := g.hidden(ids); err != nil {
700			return nil, nil, err
701		}
702		top := time.Now()
703		t0 := top
704		if err := g.head.Resize(1); err != nil {
705			return nil, nil, err
706		}
707		t0 = since(&g.Stats.Glue, t0)
708		if err := g.move.Move(g.head.InPort(), g.hc.MixedPort(), 1); err != nil {
709			return nil, nil, err
710		}
711		t0 = g.blk(&g.Stats.Move, t0)
712		if err := g.head.Run(); err != nil {
713			return nil, nil, err
714		}
715		g.blk(&g.Stats.Head, t0)
716		// The flush is where the pass actually runs, and what it takes is
717		// Stats.GPU plus the hand-over — so the clock restarts after it rather
718		// than folding a whole forward pass into the glue.
719		if err := g.flush(); err != nil {
720			return nil, nil, err
721		}
722		t0 = time.Now()
723		logits, norm = g.head.Logits(), g.hc.Mixed()
724		since(&g.Stats.Glue, t0)
725		g.Stats.Total += time.Since(top)
726		return logits, norm, nil
727	}

729	// ForwardRows runs the model over a prompt as a fresh sequence and hands
730	// every row's logits from `first` on to fn, a head-arena slab at a time.
731	//
732	// It is Forward without `inp_out_ids`, and it exists because perplexity is
733	// the one question in this vertical that needs a logit per token. The
734	// reference's graph drops every row but the last before the final mixer, so
735	// `hidden` moves one row to the front and runs the mixer and the head on it;
736	// here the mixer runs over the whole batch — it is per token, so that is the
737	// same arithmetic on nTok times the work — and the head then runs over slabs
738	// of GraphOpts.HeadRows, because a row of logits is 0.99 MB and nothing
739	// reads two of them at once.
740	//
741	// fn sees a slice into the head's mapped arena and must not keep it: the
742	// next slab overwrites it.
743	func (g *Graph) ForwardRows(ids []int32, first int, fn func(t int, logits []float32) error) error {
744		if g.head == nil {
745			return fmt.Errorf("llm: this graph was staged without a head")
746		}
747		if first < 0 || first >= len(ids) {
748			return fmt.Errorf("llm: first row %d of %d tokens", first, len(ids))
749		}
750		if err := g.Reset(); err != nil {
751			return err
752		}
753		top := time.Now()
754		g.record(len(ids))
755		if err := g.appendN(ids, g.nLayer); err != nil {
756			_ = g.flush()
757			return err
758		}
759		t0 := time.Now()
760		if err := g.hc.Run(2*g.nLayer, false); err != nil {
761			_ = g.flush()
762			return fmt.Errorf("llm: head mixer: %w", err)
763		}
764		g.blk(&g.Stats.HC, t0)
765		if err := g.flush(); err != nil {
766			return err
767		}
768	
769		// The head, a slab at a time. Each slab is its own command buffer
770		// because the logits have to be read between them, and nothing may read
771		// a device arena while a pass is being recorded (flush's one rule).
772		slab, vocab := g.head.MaxRows(), g.head.Vocab()
773		for r0 := first; r0 < len(ids); r0 += slab {
774			n := minInt(slab, len(ids)-r0)
775			g.record(n)
776			err := func() error {
777				if err := g.head.Resize(n); err != nil {
778					return err
779				}
780				if err := g.move.Move(g.head.InPort(), g.hc.MixedRowPort(r0), n); err != nil {
781					return err
782				}
783				return g.head.Run()
784			}()
785			if ferr := g.flush(); err == nil {
786				err = ferr
787			}
788			if err != nil {
789				return err
790			}
791			lg := g.head.Logits()
792			for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
793				if err := fn(r0+i, lg[i*vocab:(i+1)*vocab]); err != nil {
794					return err
795				}
796			}
797		}
798		g.Stats.Total += time.Since(top)
799		return nil
800	}

811	// HiddenExtend is Hidden without the reset: the next tokens of the sequence
812	// the graph is already holding.
813	func (g *Graph) HiddenExtend(ids []int32) ([]float32, error) {
814		top := time.Now()
815		g.record(len(ids))
816		if err := g.hidden(ids); err != nil {
817			_ = g.flush()
818			return nil, err
819		}
820		if err := g.flush(); err != nil {
821			return nil, err
822		}
823		t0 := time.Now()
824		norm := g.hc.Mixed()
825		since(&g.Stats.Glue, t0)

830	// hidden is HiddenExtend's body, without the read-back and without the
831	// submit: every layer, then the final mixer over the last token alone. It is
832	// separate so that Extend can go on recording through the head rather than
833	// flushing twice (L7d).
834	func (g *Graph) hidden(ids []int32) error {
835		if err := g.appendN(ids, g.nLayer); err != nil {
836			return err
837		}
838		top := time.Now()
839		t0 := top
840		// `inp_out_ids`: everything below is per token, so the reference drops
841		// every row but the last before the final mixer. Here that is a move of
842		// one row of the residual to the front of the same arena, and the mixer
843		// then runs as a one-token pass — the same arithmetic on 1/nTok of the
844		// work, which is what makes `result_norm` comparable against a trace
845		// that holds one row.
846		last := g.hc.ResRowPort(len(ids) - 1)
847		if err := g.hc.Resize(1); err != nil {
848			return err
849		}
850		t0 = since(&g.Stats.Glue, t0)
851		if err := g.move.Move(g.hc.ResRowPort(0), last, 1); err != nil {
852			return err
853		}
854		t0 = g.blk(&g.Stats.Move, t0)
855		if err := g.hc.Run(2*g.nLayer, false); err != nil {
856			return fmt.Errorf("llm: head mixer: %w", err)
857		}
858		g.blk(&g.Stats.HC, t0)
859		return nil
860	}

866	// `l_last-3` is the whole order — the embedding, the init, the PLE block at
867	// layer 1, three DeltaNet layers, one full-attention layer, four MoE blocks
868	// and eight mixers — for a tenth of the staging and none of the 77 GB the

870	func (g *Graph) Residual() []float32 { return g.hc.Res() }

895	// Append runs every layer over the next tokens of the sequence the graph is
896	// holding, and advances it.

898	
899	// AppendN runs the first nLayer layers over the next tokens of the sequence.
900	//
901	// Three things make this a continuation rather than a second prompt, and all
902	// three are somewhere else: the attention cache and the indexer's pooled
903	// blocks (L7a), the PLE convolution's ring (L7b), and every DeltaNet layer's
904	// recurrent state and window, which were already carried across a batch split
905	// at L3 and only ever needed the graph to stop clearing them. What is left
906	// here is the n-gram gather — a trigram, so the first token of a continuing
907	// run still reads two tokens that are not in it, which is why the graph keeps
908	// the whole id list and hashes over all of it.
909	func (g *Graph) AppendN(ids []int32, nLayer int) error {
910		top := time.Now()
911		g.record(len(ids))
912		if err := g.appendN(ids, nLayer); err != nil {
913			_ = g.flush()
914			return err
915		}
916		err := g.flush()
917		g.Stats.Total += time.Since(top)
918		return err
919	}
920	
921	// appendN is that body without the record/flush pair, for the entry points
922	// that go on recording past the layers (L7d).
923	func (g *Graph) appendN(ids []int32, nLayer int) error {
924		if nLayer <= 0 || nLayer > g.nLayer {
925			return fmt.Errorf("llm: %d layers, this graph staged %d", nLayer, g.nLayer)
926		}
927		nTok := len(ids)
928		if nTok <= 0 || nTok > g.maxTok {
929			return fmt.Errorf("llm: %d tokens, the arenas are built for %d", nTok, g.maxTok)
930		}
931		if g.past+nTok > g.nKV {
932			return fmt.Errorf("llm: %d tokens at position %d of a %d-cell context", nTok, g.past, g.nKV)
933		}
934	
935		top := time.Now()
936		t0 := top
937	
938		// The embedding gather, and the n-gram one beside it. Both are host-side
939		// reads out of the mmap'd checkpoint: `token_embd` is 675 MB of which a
940		// prompt touches nTok rows, and the n-gram table is 28.80 GB of which it
941		// touches nTok*16 — and that one has to stay on the host, because D2
942		// keeps the table off the device entirely.
943		embd, err := g.m.Embeddings(ids)
944		if err != nil {
945			return fmt.Errorf("llm: token_embd: %w", err)
946		}
947		g.ids = append(g.ids, ids...)
948		var pleEmbd []float32
949		if g.hasPLE {
950			// Hashed over the whole sequence, gathered for its tail: the trigram
951			// of the first token of this run reaches two tokens behind it.
952			rows := PLERows(g.pleCfg, g.ids)[g.past*g.pleCfg.NHeads:]
953			pleEmbd, err = g.m.PLEGather(rows, g.pleCfg.NHeads, g.pleCfg.HeadDim)
954			if err != nil {
955				return fmt.Errorf("llm: per_layer_token_embd: %w", err)
956			}
957		}
958		t0 = since(&g.Stats.Gather, t0)
959	
960		// The wide residual starts as hc identical copies of the embedding, and
961		// from here it lives in the hyper-connection block's arena: every
962		// combine updates it in place and nothing else in the graph writes it.
963		// It is per *batch* and not per sequence — the stream is a function of
964		// the token, and what carries between runs is the three histories above.
965		// This is the last host *write* of the pass — a write costs 70 GB/s
966		// where a read costs 25 (L6b-4), and the embedding is on the host
967		// anyway.
968		if err := g.hc.UploadInit(embd, nTok); err != nil {
969			return err
970		}
971		if g.attn != nil {
972			if err := g.attn.SetPast(g.past); err != nil {
973				return err
974			}
975		}
976		if g.ple != nil {
977			if err := g.ple.SetPast(g.past); err != nil {
978				return err
979			}
980		}
981		if g.dn != nil {
982			if err := g.dn.SetPast(g.past); err != nil {
983				return err
984			}
985		}
986		t0 = since(&g.Stats.Glue, t0)
987	
988		// P1a's fusion, as a scheduling rule rather than a kernel choice. A
989		// combine and the next mixer's norm are the same 2560 values per
990		// (token, stream) read, written and read again, so `RunCombineMix` does
991		// both in one dispatch — but only where nothing else touches the wide
992		// residual in between. So a combine is *held* rather than issued, and
993		// whatever comes next either absorbs it or flushes it: the PLE block,
994		// which moves the residual out of this arena and back, flushes; the end
995		// of the pass flushes, because the final mixer is reached through a row
996		// move in `hidden`. Everything else absorbs, which is 94 of the 96.
997		pending := -1
998		flushHC := func() error {
999			if pending < 0 {
1000				return nil
1001			}
1002			m := pending
1003			pending = -1
1004			return g.hc.RunCombine(m)
1005		}
1006		fuse := HCFuse()
1007		mixHC := func(m int) error {
1008			if pending < 0 {
1009				return g.hc.Run(m, false)
1010			}
1011			if !fuse {
1012				if err := flushHC(); err != nil {
1013					return err
1014				}
1015				return g.hc.Run(m, false)
1016			}
1017			p := pending
1018			pending = -1
1019			return g.hc.RunCombineMix(p, m)
1020		}
1021	
1022		for l := 0; l < nLayer; l++ {
1023			if g.hasPLE && g.pleCfg.IsPLE(l) {
1024				// The one block that reads and writes the wide residual, so the
1025				// only place the 10240-wide tensor crosses a boundary — twice,
1026				// once a graph.
1027				if err := flushHC(); err != nil {
1028					return fmt.Errorf("llm: layer %d ple combine: %w", l, err)
1029				}
1030				t0 = g.blk(&g.Stats.HC, t0)
1031				if err := g.ple.UploadEmbd(pleEmbd, nTok); err != nil {
1032					return err
1033				}
1034				t0 = since(&g.Stats.Glue, t0)
1035				if err := g.move.Move(g.ple.ResPort(), g.hc.ResPort(), nTok); err != nil {
1036					return err
1037				}
1038				t0 = g.blk(&g.Stats.Move, t0)
1039				if err := g.ple.Run(); err != nil {
1040					return err
1041				}
1042				t0 = g.blk(&g.Stats.PLE, t0)
1043				if err := g.move.Move(g.hc.ResPort(), g.ple.ResPort(), nTok); err != nil {
1044					return err
1045				}
1046				t0 = g.blk(&g.Stats.Move, t0)
1047			}
1048	
1049			// The attention half.
1050			if err := mixHC(2 * l); err != nil {
1051				return fmt.Errorf("llm: layer %d attn mix: %w", l, err)
1052			}
1053			t0 = g.blk(&g.Stats.HC, t0)
1054			t1, err := g.sublayer(l, nTok, t0)
1055			if err != nil {
1056				return err
1057			}
1058			t0 = t1
1059			pending = 2 * l
1060	
1061			// The FFN half, which every layer has.
1062			if err := mixHC(2*l + 1); err != nil {
1063				return fmt.Errorf("llm: layer %d ffn mix: %w", l, err)
1064			}
1065			t0 = g.blk(&g.Stats.HC, t0)
1066			if err := g.moe.Resize(nTok); err != nil {
1067				return err
1068			}
1069			t0 = since(&g.Stats.Glue, t0)
1070			if err := g.move.Move(g.moe.InPort(), g.hc.MixedPort(), nTok); err != nil {
1071				return err
1072			}
1073			t0 = g.blk(&g.Stats.Move, t0)
1074			if err := g.moe.Run(l); err != nil {
1075				return fmt.Errorf("llm: layer %d moe: %w", l, err)
1076			}
1077			t0 = g.blk(&g.Stats.MoE, t0)
1078			if err := g.move.Move(g.hc.BlockOutPort(), g.moe.OutPort(), nTok); err != nil {
1079				return err
1080			}
1081			t0 = g.blk(&g.Stats.Move, t0)
1082			pending = 2*l + 1
1083		}
1084		if err := flushHC(); err != nil {
1085			return fmt.Errorf("llm: last combine: %w", err)
1086		}
1087		t0 = g.blk(&g.Stats.HC, t0)
1088		g.past += nTok
1089		g.Stats.Runs++
1090		return nil
1091	}

1093	// sublayer runs one layer's attention half — the gated DeltaNet in 36 layers
1094	// of 48, full attention with the QSA indexer in the other 12 — leaving its
1095	// output in the hyper-connection block's arena for the combine, and returning
1096	// the clock it left off at.
1097	//
1098	// Nothing here is a host tensor. The mixer's output is moved into the layer's
1099	// fp16 A operand by one dispatch and the layer's output is moved back by
1100	// another; `Resize` is only the length of the run and whatever a Move will
1101	// not reach.
1102	func (g *Graph) sublayer(l, nTok int, t0 time.Time) (time.Time, error) {
1103		k := g.kinds[l]
1104		var in, out Port
1105		var run func() error
1106		if k.attn {
1107			if err := g.attn.Resize(nTok); err != nil {
1108				return t0, err
1109			}
1110			in, out = g.attn.InPort(), g.attn.OutPort()
1111			run = func() error { return g.attn.Run(k.idx) }
1112		} else {
1113			if err := g.dn.Resize(nTok); err != nil {
1114				return t0, err
1115			}
1116			in, out = g.dn.InPort(), g.dn.OutPort()
1117			run = func() error { return g.dn.Run(k.idx) }
1118		}
1119		t0 = since(&g.Stats.Glue, t0)
1120		if err := g.move.Move(in, g.hc.MixedPort(), nTok); err != nil {
1121			return t0, err
1122		}
1123		t0 = g.blk(&g.Stats.Move, t0)
1124		if err := run(); err != nil {
1125			return t0, fmt.Errorf("llm: layer %d sublayer: %w", l, err)
1126		}
1127		if k.attn {
1128			t0 = g.blk(&g.Stats.Attn, t0)
1129		} else {
1130			t0 = g.blk(&g.Stats.DeltaNet, t0)
1131		}
1132		if err := g.move.Move(g.hc.BlockOutPort(), out, nTok); err != nil {
1133			return t0, err
1134		}
1135		return g.blk(&g.Stats.Move, t0), nil
1136	}

3	// L6b's gate: the five blocks in order, against llama.cpp's own logits.
4	//
5	// Every test before this one fed a block llama.cpp's value for the tensor it
6	// reads, so a disagreement was that block's. Here the only input is the token
7	// list: everything else is ours, and the tolerance has to hold error that
8	// accumulated through 48 layers of five block types rather than through one.
9	//
10	//	go test ./llm/ -v -run TestGraphPrefix   # four layers, ~3 s
11	//	go test ./llm/ -v -run TestGraphLogits   # all 48, 85 GB, ~40 s
12	//
13	// The prefix test is the one to run while the order is being changed. It
14	// stages four layers against `l_last-3` — which is the whole shape of the
15	// graph, PLE block and full-attention layer included, because the interval is
16	// four — and needs 7 GB instead of 85.
17	//
18	// The depth column both of them print is `reference/out/llmdepth/`, a second
19	// pass of the oracle over the same prompt filtered to `l_last` every eight
20	// layers. It exists because a single deep number is not evidence: 0.5% at the
21	// bottom of 48 layers is either accumulation or a bug, and only the shape of
22	// the curve between here and there tells them apart.
23	
24	import (
25		"fmt"
26		"sort"
27		"testing"
28		"time"
29	)
30	
31	// depthDir is the second pass of the oracle: `l_last` every eight layers of
32	// the same seven-token prompt, plus the head's two tensors.
33	//
34	//	/tmp/eval_dump -m $M -o reference/out/llmdepth -c 64 \
35	//	    -p 'The capital of France is Paris.' \
36	//	    -n '^l_last-(7|15|23|31|39|47)$|^result_(norm|output)$'
37	const depthDir = "../reference/out/llmdepth"
38	
39	// graphFixture stages a graph over the 7-token trace's prompt.
40	func graphFixture(t *testing.T, opts GraphOpts) (*Graph, *Trace, []int32) {
41		t.Helper()
42		m, tr := fixtures(t)
43		ids, prompt, err := tr.Tokens()
44		if err != nil {
45			t.Fatal(err)
46		}
47		dev, done := newTestDevice(t)
48		t.Cleanup(done)
49	
50		opts.MaxTokens = len(ids)
51		start := time.Now()
52		g, err := NewGraph(dev, m, opts)
53		if err != nil {
54			t.Fatal(err)
55		}
56		t.Cleanup(g.Destroy)
57	
58		var w, a, bufs int
59		for _, s := range g.Staged {
60			t.Logf("  %-11s %2d layers %4d buffers %8.2f GB %8.1f MB %8s",
61				s.Name, s.Layers, s.Buffers, float64(s.Weights)/1e9, float64(s.Arenas)/1e6,
62				s.Elapsed.Round(time.Millisecond))
63			w, a, bufs = w+s.Weights, a+s.Arenas, bufs+s.Buffers
64		}
65		t.Logf("%d layers, %d tokens (%q), %.2f GB of weights and %.2f GB of arenas in %d buffers, staged in %s",
66			g.Layers(), len(ids), prompt, float64(w)/1e9, float64(a)/1e9, bufs,
67			time.Since(start).Round(time.Millisecond))
68		return g, tr, ids
69	}
70	
71	// TestGraphPrefix runs the first four layers and checks the residual against
72	// `l_last-3`.
73	//
74	// Four is the whole architecture: layers 0, 1 and 2 are the gated DeltaNet,
75	// layer 1 has the PLE n-gram block in front of it, layer 3 is the first
76	// full-attention layer with the QSA indexer, and all four have a MoE block.
77	// So an order that is wrong anywhere is wrong here, at 9 GB and a minute
78	// rather than 85 GB and thirty-three seconds of staging.
79	func TestGraphPrefix(t *testing.T) {
80		const layers = 4
81		g, tr, ids := graphFixture(t, GraphOpts{Layers: layers, NoHead: true})
82	
83		// One depth per dumped `l_last`, off the same staged model. The point is
84		// the *trend*: L6b's only deep comparison is at layer 47, and whether
85		// 0.5% there is accumulation or a bug is a question this column answers
86		// and a single number cannot.
87		var last cmpResult
88		for n := 1; n <= layers; n++ {
89			if err := g.PrefillN(ids, n); err != nil {
90				t.Fatal(err)
91			}
92			want, err := tr.Get(fmt.Sprintf("l_last-%d", n-1), 0)
93			if err != nil {
94				t.Fatal(err)
95			}
96			r, err := compare(g.Residual(), want.Vals)
97			if err != nil {
98				t.Fatal(err)
99			}
100			t.Logf("l_last-%d over %d tokens: %v  (%.3f%% of scale)",
101				n-1, len(ids), r, 100*r.rms/r.refMax)
102			last = r
103		}
104		// The residual is a sum of four layers of block output on top of the
105		// embedding, and every one of those went through a Q8_0 matmul with an
106		// fp16 accumulator (L4a-5). The per-block gates this repeats are 1e-4 to
107		// 1e-3 rms on their own outputs.
108		if last.rms > 5e-3 {
109			t.Errorf("l_last-%d: rms %.3e over 5e-3 (%v)", layers-1, last.rms, last)
110		}
111	}

189	    // **Continuing a sequence needs three more fields and the block has
190	    // none** (L7). 64 uints is 256 bytes and that is this device's whole
191	    // push-constant range, so the things a run that follows another knows
192	    // that a fresh one does not are said by fields their blocks already do
193	    // not use — the same arrangement `moeUsed` documents above, and the same
194	    // rule: the mapping lives here, and nothing spells the borrowed field's
195	    // own name.
196	    //
197	    //   lowRank   SEQ_PAST:    tokens of this sequence already behind the
198	    //             run. For the attention layer that is cells in the KV cache,
199	    //             so token t is cell SEQ_PAST + t at position SEQ_PAST + t;
200	    //             for the PLE block it is how far back its convolution may
201	    //             reach. Zero is a fresh sequence. Only the hyper-connection
202	    //             block uses `lowRank` as itself.
203	    //   injOff    SEQ_HIST:    the ring a convolution over the token axis
204	    //             reads behind itself, addressed by **position modulo its
205	    //             length**: f32 [(kern-1)*dil][hc*nEmbd] for the PLE block,
206	    //             f32 [kern-1][gemmN] per layer for the gated DeltaNet.
207	    //             `injOff` is the hyper-connection block's scatter weights
208	    //             and neither of those blocks has any.
209	    //   loOff     SEQ_SRC:     the tensor llm_seq_hist.comp copies those rows
210	    //             *out* of, for the one dispatch that writes the ring. It is
211	    //             the same field ATTN_IDXRAW is, because the two are never
212	    //             in the same push block: one is the attention layer's and
213	    //             the other belongs to the two convolutions.
214	    //   loOff     ATTN_IDXRAW: fp16 [nKV][idxDim], the indexer's *raw* key
215	    //             per cell. It is a cache because a pooled block spans
216	    //             `ratio` cells and at decode those arrive in `ratio`
217	    //             different batches; llm_attn_pack.comp writes this batch's
218	    //             cells and llm_attn_idx.comp pools out of it.
219	    //
220	    // kOff, vOff and idxKOff are unchanged as fields and changed as tensors:
221	    // they now address **one staged layer's** cache rather than a shared
222	    // arena, because a cache belongs to the layer that filled it. The key and
223	    // value planes are nKV cells rather than `plane` token rows; idxKOff is
224	    // the pooled table, and a block that is already complete is never
225	    // recomputed.
226	
227	    // The gated DeltaNet (llm_dn_conv.comp, llm_dn_scan.comp,
228	    // llm_dn_norm.comp). Thirty-six of the 48 layers, and the only ones with
229	    // a recurrent state.
230	    //
231	    // Six fields, because the rest of this block already says what the layer
232	    // needs: `qkvOff` is the one fused projection again ([q | k | v | z |
233	    // alpha | beta], six of llama.cpp's four matrices), `gemmN` its row
234	    // stride, `convOff`/`kern` the depthwise taps as the PLE block states
235	    // them, `normOff` the convolution's normalised output, `outOff` the
236	    // recurrence's, `ctxOff` the fp16 A operand of the output projection,
237	    // `gammaOff` the shared head norm and `heads`/`kvHeads`/`headDim` the
238	    // 48/16/128 the whole layer is shaped around.
239	    uint ssmGateOff;  // f32 [T][heads]: the log decay, softplus(a)*A
240	    uint ssmBetaOff;  // f32 [T][heads]: sigmoid(beta)
241	    uint ssmStateOff; // f32 [heads][headDim][headDim], s[h][j][i] = S[i][j]
242	    uint ssmAOff;     // f32 [heads]: ssm_a, already -exp(A_log)
243	    uint ssmDTOff;    // f32 [heads]: ssm_dt.bias
244	    uint ssmNorm;     // 1 = ggml_l2_norm's max(|x|, eps), 0 = #28068's rsqrt
245	
246	    // The MoE block (llm_moe_route.comp, llm_moe_perm.comp,
247	    // llm_moe_gemm.comp, llm_moe_combine.comp). Every one of the 48 layers
248	    // has one, 97% of the checkpoint's parameters are in them, and L2a put
249	    // them at 35.7% of the prefill graph.
250	    //
251	    // **Five fields, and the block is out of room**: 64 uints is 256 bytes,
252	    // which is this device's whole push-constant range. So the rest of what
253	    // the MoE needs is said by fields that already mean it, and the mapping
254	    // is written down here rather than inferred at four call sites:
255	    //
256	    //   xnOff/lda     the block's fp16 input, [T][lda] -- the A operand of
257	    //                 the router and of every routed gate/up tile
258	    //   qkvOff        f32 [T][gemmN]: the one fused projection's output
259	    //                 again, which here is the router's 512 logits with the
260	    //                 shared expert's one-column gate as a 513th
261	    //   ctxOff/ldCtx  fp16 [rows][ffn]: silu(gate)*up, which is exactly what
262	    //                 that field already is -- the A operand of the layer's
263	    //                 output projection
264	    //   gatedOff      f32 [T][used+1][nEmbd]: "value * gate", which here is
265	    //                 the down projection's output times its routing weight,
266	    //                 one row per (token, slot) and the last slot the shared
267	    //                 expert's
268	    //   outOff        f32 [T][nEmbd]: ffn_out, the block's output
269	    //   bOff          the **byte** offset of a dispatch's first quantised
270	    //                 matrix in the bank above -- `gate` for a swiglu tile,
271	    //                 `down` for a down tile
272	    //   gemmM         the row block the tile list is cut to, which the
273	    //                 permutation kernel has to know and every GEMM rung
274	    //                 compiles in
275	    //   gemmN         the bank's output width per expert, so that expert e's
276	    //                 output row n is bank row e*gemmN + n -- and, for the
277	    //                 route and permutation kernels, the expert count
278	    //   gemmK         the reduction extent, which is also what says how many
279	    //                 quantised blocks a row holds
280	    uint moePermOff;   // uint: topk[T][used], then the expert-major permutation
281	    uint moeTileOff;   // uint: the tile count, the per-expert counts, offsets
282	                       // and tile bases, then 3 uints per (expert, row block)
283	    uint moeWeightOff; // f32 [T][used+1]: the normalised routing weights, and
284	                       // sigmoid(shared_expert_gate) in the last slot
285	
286	    uint moeBOff2;     // the byte offset of a swiglu tile's second matrix, `up`
287	    // Experts per token in the low sixteen bits -- the slot stride is that
288	    // plus one -- and the **bank index** in the high sixteen.
289	    //

291	    // was room for: 64 uints is 256 bytes and that is this device's whole
292	    // push-constant range. L6a's array of bank buffers needs a layer index at
293	    // every GEMM dispatch and there is no 65th field to put it in, so it goes

1	// Shared binding and push-constant layout for the qwen3.8-flash-next
2	// kernels (LLM.md L2).
3	//
4	// Same four-arena arrangement the DiT and the text encoder use
5	// (dit_common.glsl): one fp32 weight arena, one fp32 activation arena, one
6	// fp16 activation arena and one fp16 weight bank, with "which tensor"
7	// expressed as an offset so that a whole block is a dispatch sequence over
8	// one descriptor set. vk.DispatchMultiTimed records a sequence into a single
9	// command buffer only if every pipeline in it was built over the same buffers
10	// with the same push-constant size, so the block below is one size for every
11	// kernel in this vertical.
12	//
13	// It is a separate file from dit_common.glsl rather than a reuse of it
14	// because the fields are a contract with a *shader*, and a hyper-connection
15	// block has no heads, no head dim and no rotary table, while it does have a
16	// stream count, a low rank and three activation tensors that do not exist
17	// anywhere else. Naming one of those `span` or `aux1` is how a graph gets
18	// silently wrong (the reason zimage/qwen keeps its own copy of the DiT's).
19	
20	layout(binding = 0) readonly buffer Weights { float wbuf[]; };
21	layout(binding = 1) buffer Act { float act[]; };
22	layout(binding = 2) buffer HAct { float16_t hact[]; };
23	layout(binding = 3) readonly buffer W16 { float16_t w16[]; };
24	// The fp32 activation arena again, read as uints. The QSA selection is a
25	// bitmask — one bit per cache cell per token — and a bitmask is not a float:
26	// punning it through `uintBitsToFloat` would put NaN payloads in a storage
27	// buffer and trust them to survive, where binding the same VkBuffer at a
28	// second descriptor costs nothing and says what the tensor is. Every pipeline
29	// in this vertical declares it so that a sequence can still be recorded into
30	// one command buffer; only llm_attn_select.comp writes it and only
31	// llm_attn_wmma.comp reads it.
32	layout(binding = 4) buffer ActU { uint actu[]; };
33	// The quantised expert bank, read as raw words. **Only the MoE block
34	// declares it** (`-DMOE_QBANK`), because every other kernel in this vertical
35	// is built over five buffers and a shader that names a binding its descriptor
36	// set does not have is a pipeline that will not create.
37	//
38	// It is `uint` and not `float16_t` for the reason L5b exists: one layer's
39	// three expert banks are 2.52 billion weights, 5.03 GB dequantised to halves
40	// and 75 GB across the model, so they stay in the checkpoint's own Q4_K, Q5_K,
41	// Q5_1 and Q8_0 blocks and the kernel unpacks its own slab per K-step. A
42	// tensor is addressed by its **byte** offset here, not its element offset,
43	// because a Q8_0 block is 34 bytes and nothing about these formats is
44	// four-aligned below the row.
45	#ifdef MOE_QBANK
46	// **It is an array of buffers, one a layer.** `maxStorageBufferRange` on this
47	// device is 4 GiB - 4 and the whole bank is 77 GB (LLM.md L6a), so residency
48	// is not a matter of one arena with a per-layer offset: a layer's 1.61 GB is
49	// a buffer of its own, all NBANK of them are bound at one binding, and the
50	// layer index selects. The index is dynamically uniform — one layer per
51	// dispatch — so this is core Vulkan and not descriptor indexing.
52	#ifndef NBANK
53	#define NBANK 1
54	#endif
55	layout(binding = 5) readonly buffer QBank { uint w[]; } qb[NBANK];
56	// The same buffer again, as sixteen-byte words. A Q4_K super-block is 144
57	// bytes and a Q5_K one 176, both multiples of sixteen, so the 32 bytes of
58	// nibbles a lane unpacks per K-step are two aligned `uvec4` loads where they
59	// would otherwise be eight `uint` ones — and this kernel turned out to be
60	// bound by how many load instructions its unpack issues, not by the bytes
61	// they fetch. Q5_1's 24-byte and Q8_0's 34-byte blocks are not aligned to
62	// sixteen and go on reading the `uint` view.
63	layout(binding = 6) readonly buffer QBank4 { uvec4 w[]; } qb4[NBANK];
64	// The kernel goes on spelling them `qbank` and `qbank4`: which buffer of the
65	// array is the same fact for every load a dispatch issues, so it belongs at
66	// the declaration rather than at the 30-odd call sites.
67	#define qbank  qb[MOE_BANK].w
68	#define qbank4 qb4[MOE_BANK].w
69	#endif
70	
71	// The **dense** weight bank read as raw words: LLM.md L8.
72	//
73	// Binding 3 above is the same buffer as halves, and for every kernel written
74	// before L8 that is all it is. L8's bank is not halves: a dense weight is
75	// staged as the checkpoint's own int8 with one fp16 scale per 32 elements of
76	// a row — 8.5 bits a weight against 16 — because at decode a token reads
77	// 8.07 GB of dense weight against the 3.67 the checkpoint ships, and that
78	// ratio *is* the decode rate (L7c-5). So the tiles are bytes and the scales
79	// are halves, in one buffer, and the buffer is bound twice: `w8` for the
80	// tiles and `w16` for the plane that follows them.
81	//
82	// It takes binding 5 because a dense kernel is never a MoE kernel — the two
83	// `#ifdef`s below are mutually exclusive and nothing declares both — and
84	// because every pipeline in a recorded sequence carries its own descriptor
85	// set, so a build that names six buffers may sit beside one that names five.
86	//
87	// **L8c-4 narrows it again and the binding does not change.** The 4.5-bit
88	// bank is nibble tiles plus a sixteen-byte ggml record per (column,
89	// super-block), so `w8` is the whole of it as raw words there too — the two
90	// `-D`s name which bank a build reads and both bind the same way.
91	#if defined(DENSE_Q8) || defined(DENSE_Q4)
92	layout(binding = 5) readonly buffer W8 { uint w8[]; };
93	#endif
94	
95	layout(push_constant) uniform PC {
96	    // The wide residual, fp32 in the activation arena: [T][hc*nEmbd], which
97	    // is ggml's [nEmbd, hc, T] read the same way round (ne[0] is fastest).
98	    uint resOff;
99	    // The normalised activation, fp16: [T][lda], stream c at column c*nEmbd.

540	func (g *AttnGPU) alloc(nLayers int) error {
541		c := g.cfg
542		rows := g.arenaRows
543		rotHalf := c.RopeDims / 2
544	
545		// fp32 weights: four gammas a layer, then one rotary table for all of them.
546		perLayer := 2*c.HeadDim + 2*c.IdxDim
547		g.wElems = nLayers*perLayer + 2*g.nKV*rotHalf
548		g.wRope = uint32(nLayers * perLayer)
549		var err error
550		if g.wbuf, err = g.dev.NewBuffer(g.wElems * 4); err != nil {
551			return fmt.Errorf("llm: attention fp32 weight arena: %w", err)
552		}
553	
554		alloc := func(n int) uint32 {
555			off := uint32(g.actElems)
556			g.actElems += (n + 63) &^ 63
557			return off
558		}
559		g.aQKV = alloc(rows * g.qkvN())
560		g.aScore = alloc(rows * g.NBlocks())
561		g.aCell = alloc(rows * g.nKV)
562		// The output gets its own arena rather than being written back over the
563		// projection's. It is 5 MB at 512 tokens against the 27 the fused
564		// projection holds, and aliasing them would cost the layer's own inputs —
565		// which at L6 the residual add still wants — to save that.
566		g.aOut = alloc(rows * c.NEmbd)
567		// The bitmask is allocated for every arena row, not just the prompt's,
568		// because the attention kernel's pad rows index it — they read it as dense
569		// rather than branching, and an unallocated row would be a read past the
570		// buffer.
571		g.aSel = alloc(rows * g.selWords())
572		// The decode GEMV's partial sums, f32 [KSLABS][gemmN] (L8e-1). The wider
573		// of the two projections is the fused one, so 40 x 13952 x 4 = 2.2 MB —
574		// allocated whichever rung runs, because the arena plan is fixed at
575		// construction and the rung is not.
576		g.aPart = alloc(gemvMaxSlabs * g.qkvN())
577		if g.abuf, err = newArena(g.dev, g.actElems*4); err != nil {
578			return fmt.Errorf("llm: attention fp32 activation arena (%d MB): %w", (g.actElems*4)>>20, err)
579		}
580	
581		halloc := func(n int) uint32 {
582			off := uint32(g.hElems)
583			g.hElems += (n + 63) &^ 63
584			return off
585		}
586		plane := rows * c.HeadDim
587		g.hXn = halloc(rows * g.lda)
588		g.hQ = halloc(c.NHead * plane)
589		g.hCtx = halloc(rows * g.ldCtx)
590		g.hIdxQ = halloc(rows * c.IdxHeads * c.IdxDim)
591	
592		// The cache, one plane a layer. A query plane is padded token *rows* of
593		// one batch; a key plane is the layer's nKV *cells* and outlives it, so
594		// the two geometries part company here and the shaders are told both.
595		//
596		// It is 2.31 KB a cell a layer — 1 KB of key, 1 KB of value, 256 B of the
597		// indexer's raw key and 64 B of its pooled block — so twelve layers are
598		// 27.7 KB a cell: 57 MB at 2048 cells, 906 MB at 32768. The one structural
599		// limit is that it shares a buffer with the arenas above and
600		// `maxStorageBufferRange` is 4 GiB - 4, which caps this at about 148k
601		// cells; past that the cache wants L6a's array-of-buffers, one a layer.
602		g.kvStride = c.NHeadKV * g.nKV * c.HeadDim
603		g.idxRawStride = g.nKV * c.IdxDim
604		g.idxKStride = g.NBlocks() * c.IdxDim
605		g.hK = halloc(nLayers * g.kvStride)
606		g.hV = halloc(nLayers * g.kvStride)
607		g.hIdxRaw = halloc(nLayers * g.idxRawStride)
608		g.hIdxK = halloc(nLayers * g.idxKStride)
609		if g.hbuf, err = newArena(g.dev, g.hElems*2); err != nil {
610			return fmt.Errorf("llm: attention fp16 activation arena (%d MB): %w", (g.hElems*2)>>20, err)
611		}
612		// Zeroed once: every A operand's pad columns and every short run's pad
613		// rows come from here, and none of these kernels bounds-check.
614		g.hbuf.Zero()

     moved out of the push constants to make that legal, and the two host

[← LLM.md](../LLM.md) · [← LLM2.md](../LLM2.md) · [research index](README.md) · [P1](p1-decode-attribution.md) · [P1a](p1a-hyper-connection-shape.md) · [P1b](p1b-moe-decode-rescreen.md) · phase 2

# P1c — the decode step, recorded once: 1.90 ms of the priced 1.96, and the machine moved more than the fix

**Result: the decode step is one pre-recorded command buffer, replayed with a
fence per token, and it is worth its estimate.** P1 priced idea 2 at 1.127 ms
of host recording plus 0.828 ms of hand-over — 1.96 ms, 6.4% of the step —
and on matched machine state the fix returns **1.90 ms a token**: 39.39 →
37.50 ms a step, **25.4 → 26.7 tok/s**, the `record` row 1.127 → 0.16-0.17 ms
and the hand-over 0.82 → 0.25. Two runs each arm, 0.03% apart. The gate is
bit-level: 48 greedy tokens *and all 48 full logit rows* identical to the
re-recording arm on the four-layer prefix, the whole model's greedy text
identical to EOG, and prefill at ubatch 2048 unregressed (1070.3 against the
baseline binary's 1061.5 the same hour).

**And the reason every number above is quoted against a same-day control:
the machine moved 8.7 ms a step overnight with nothing changed.** Yesterday's
binary, byte for byte, measured 30.51 ms a step for P1b and measures 39.20
today. See the last section.

## The premise, measured first

The whole idea rests on the decode graph being shape-stable, so the first
thing built was the instrument (`TestDecodeDispatchDiff`): capture the
recorded sequence of consecutive one-token passes and diff them dispatch for
dispatch — pipeline, grid, and every push-constant dword, mapped back to its
field name by reflection over the `push` block. Over 40 steps on the
four-layer prefix:

- **Every pipeline, every grid, every label, in the same order, every step.**
- **111 of 131 dispatches carried identical push constants already.**
- The other 20 differed in exactly **one dword: `lowRank`, carrying the
  sequence position** — twelve kinds (`attn.pack/idx/score/attn`,
  `dn.conv/hist/norm/scan`, `ple.conv/gate/hist/kv`), of which only seven
  shaders actually read it (`SEQ_PAST`); the rest carried it because their
  block's base push block did.

So the entire varying state of a decode step was one uint. The token id never
touches a push constant or a grid — it enters through the arenas the host
writes (the embedding rows, the n-gram gather).

## Finding 1 — the position moves into the arena, and the step becomes bytes

`SEQ_PAST` is now **dword 0 of each block's own fp32 activation arena**, read
through the `actu` view every pipeline already binds (`actu[0]`), written by
each block's `SetPast` as a 4-byte mapped write. It is the first allocation
of the three sequence-carrying blocks (attention, DeltaNet, PLE), asserted at
offset zero because the shaders hardcode it; the `lowRank` field stays zero
in those blocks' base push blocks and keeps its other meanings elsewhere (the
hyper-connection's actual low rank, the GEMV rungs' int8 split). One macro
changed in `llm_common.glsl`; nine `.spv` recompiled; no pipeline layout, no
new binding, no spec constant.

After the change the diff instrument reports **131 of 131 dispatches
byte-identical over 40 steps**, and every SEQ_PAST-consuming gate passes
unchanged: the cache-is-a-chunk-split tests, the pooled-block tests, the
selection tests at 4k, the graph chunk-split, `TestGraphPrefix`.

Why not a uniform buffer? The push block is 64 uints — this device's whole
range — and full; a new binding would have re-cut every descriptor layout for
one uint. Dword 0 of a buffer every kernel already binds costs one scalar
load that ACO hoists, and nothing else.

## Finding 2 — record once, replay with a fence

`vk.Prerecorded` (shim: `shim_prerecord_multi` / `shim_submit_prerecorded`)
records the same sequence `DispatchMultiMarked` would — same barriers, same
per-dispatch timestamps, the query-pool reset *inside* the command buffer so
the marks re-arm on every submit — into its own command pool, once. Submit is
a fence reset, one `vkQueueSubmit`, a fence wait and the timestamp read.
Because the marks survive, **`-gen -attrib` works identically on the replay
path**, which is how the table below exists.

The graph captures at the first one-token `Extend` with `past > 0` — the
capture *is* the sequence that token submitted, taken at flush before the
recorder resets — and replays from the second token on
(`extendPrerecorded`): the two gathers, the uploads, the `SetPast`s and the
host-side `Resize(1)`s (field sets and pad clears, kept because a pass after
a fresh prefill would otherwise run with the prompt's row count in host
state), then one submit of all **1407 dispatches in one buffer** where the
live path chunks into two (27 ms of GPU against the watchdog's 2 s; the
recording sizes its own query pool). `past > 0` because a fresh sequence is a
different shape: at position zero the attention block rebuilds its whole
pooled table and `attn.idx`'s grid is NBlocks, not one. `PinSchedule` drops
the capture; `LLM_NO_PRERECORD=1` is the control arm.

## The step, before and after (same machine state, same hour)

64 greedy tokens, whole model, shipped bank. Control is `LLM_NO_PRERECORD=1`;
`baseline` is yesterday's binary rebuilt from HEAD in a worktree.

| arm | ms/step | tok/s | record | hand-over | dispatches (GPU) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| baseline binary (P1b's code) | 39.20 | 25.51 | 1.111 | 0.824 | 35.88 |
| control (this code, re-recording) | 39.39 | 25.38 | 1.127 | 0.822 | 35.93 |
| **prerecorded** | **37.50 / 37.49** | **26.68 / 26.70** | **0.171 / 0.160** | **0.259 / 0.249** | 35.59 / 35.57 |

Three things worth saying:

- **The control equals the baseline.** Phase A (the arena slot, the shifted
  arena offsets, the buffer-read `SEQ_PAST` in seven kernels) costs nothing
  measurable — decode or prefill (1070.3 vs 1061.5 tok/s at ubatch 2048,
  new code faster within noise).
- **The win is 1.90 of the priced 1.96 ms.** What remains in the two rows is
  real work the fix never claimed: ~0.16 ms of per-token uploads (the
  embedding rows, the n-gram slab, the pads) that used to hide inside
  `record`, and ~0.25 ms of one submit + fence, which is the floor for
  handing anything to the GPU. The `record` row's *recording* — building
  push constants for 1407 dispatches and the cgo command encoding — is gone.
- **On P1b's machine state this is ~28.6 ms a step, ~34.9 tok/s** — the
  +2.2 tok/s P1 priced — but that state was not available to measure (below),
  so the claim stays arithmetic and the measured claim is +1.3 tok/s on a
  day when the whole step was 29% slower.

`results/p1c_decode_attrib.csv` is the prerecorded arm's full table.

## Finding 3 — the environment moved 8.7 ms overnight, and it names its kernels

P1b ended with a measured **1.33 ms environment gap** and the note that a
dispatch inside a step is 8-22% slower than alone on a cold bank. Today the
environment demonstrated a much larger degree of freedom: **yesterday's
binary, unchanged, measures 39.20 ms a step where it measured 30.51** — and
the inflation is not uniform:

| label | P1b, us | today, us | ratio |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| dn.qkv | 114.9 | 206.2 | 1.79 |
| head.head | 1964 | 3531 | 1.80 |
| attn.qkv | 95.6 | 181.9 | 1.90 |
| dn.out | 45.9 | 72.8 | 1.59 |
| hc.up | 16.8 | 26.2 | 1.56 |
| moe.up | 106.9 | 108.9 | **1.02** |
| moe.down | 72.2 | 69.8 | **0.97** |

fence per token, and it is worth its estimate.** P1 priced idea 2 at 1.127 ms

identical to EOG, and prefill at ubatch 2048 unregressed (1070.3 against the
baseline binary's 1061.5 the same hour).

the machine moved 8.7 ms a step overnight with nothing changed.** Yesterday's
binary, byte for byte, measured 30.51 ms a step for P1b and measures 39.20
today. See the last section.

## The premise, measured first

The whole idea rests on the decode graph being shape-stable, so the first
thing built was the instrument (`TestDecodeDispatchDiff`): capture the
recorded sequence of consecutive one-token passes and diff them dispatch for
dispatch — pipeline, grid, and every push-constant dword, mapped back to its
field name by reflection over the `push` block. Over 40 steps on the
four-layer prefix:

- **Every pipeline, every grid, every label, in the same order, every step.**
- **111 of 131 dispatches carried identical push constants already.**

  sequence position** — twelve kinds (`attn.pack/idx/score/attn`,
  `dn.conv/hist/norm/scan`, `ple.conv/gate/hist/kv`), of which only seven
  shaders actually read it (`SEQ_PAST`); the rest carried it because their
  block's base push block did.

So the entire varying state of a decode step was one uint. The token id never
touches a push constant or a grid — it enters through the arenas the host
writes (the embedding rows, the n-gram gather).

## Finding 1 — the position moves into the arena, and the step becomes bytes

`SEQ_PAST` is now **dword 0 of each block's own fp32 activation arena**, read
through the `actu` view every pipeline already binds (`actu[0]`), written by
each block's `SetPast` as a 4-byte mapped write. It is the first allocation
of the three sequence-carrying blocks (attention, DeltaNet, PLE), asserted at
offset zero because the shaders hardcode it; the `lowRank` field stays zero
in those blocks' base push blocks and keeps its other meanings elsewhere (the
hyper-connection's actual low rank, the GEMV rungs' int8 split). One macro
changed in `llm_common.glsl`; nine `.spv` recompiled; no pipeline layout, no
new binding, no spec constant.

byte-identical over 40 steps**, and every SEQ_PAST-consuming gate passes
unchanged: the cache-is-a-chunk-split tests, the pooled-block tests, the
selection tests at 4k, the graph chunk-split, `TestGraphPrefix`.

Why not a uniform buffer? The push block is 64 uints — this device's whole
range — and full; a new binding would have re-cut every descriptor layout for
one uint. Dword 0 of a buffer every kernel already binds costs one scalar
load that ACO hoists, and nothing else.

`vk.Prerecorded` (shim: `shim_prerecord_multi` / `shim_submit_prerecorded`)
records the same sequence `DispatchMultiMarked` would — same barriers, same
per-dispatch timestamps, the query-pool reset *inside* the command buffer so
